title: PRESIDENT OF INDIA INAUGURATES THE YEAR-LONG GOLDEN JUBILEE CELEBRATIONS OF INDIAN COUNCIL OF MEDICAL RESEARCH-NATIONAL INSTITUTE OF MALARIA RESEARCH
subtitle: PREMIER INSTITUTIONS LIKE THE ICMR CAN TAKE THE LEAD IN ACHIEVING THE HEALTH-RELATED GOALS OF VIKSIT BHARAT THROUGH RESEARCH, COLLABORATION AND INNOVATION: PRESIDENT DROUPADI MURMU
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                17 NOV 2026 2:58PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The President of India, Smt Droupadi Murmu inaugurated the year-long Golden Jubilee Celebrations of the Indian Council of Medical Research-National Institute of Malaria Research in New Delhi today (November 17, 2026).
Speaking on the occasion, the President said that malaria has long been a serious public health challenge in many countries around the world, including India. At the time of independence, it was one of the most critical public health challenges in our country. It is a matter of satisfaction that India has made remarkable progress in malaria control over the last few years. Improved healthcare services, modern diagnostic techniques, effective medicines, mosquito-control campaigns, and community participation have played a significant role in curbing the spread of this disease. India’s progress toward malaria elimination has received global recognition. In 2024, India moved out of the World Health Organization’s ‘High Burden to High Impact’ category. This achievement has been made possible through the collective efforts of our public health programs, scientists, healthcare workers, and citizens. The National Institute of Malaria Research has played a pivotal role in this long battle against malaria. Over the past five decades, it has conducted pioneering research in areas such as malaria parasites, mosquitoes, vector control, insecticide resistance, and community-based surveillance.
The President said that new challenges, such as climate change, unplanned urbanization, and the growing resistance of mosquitoes to insecticides, could pose fresh obstacles to the eradication of malaria. In such a scenario, the efforts of healthcare workers alone cannot prevent the spread of malaria. It is also necessary to focus on preventing water stagnation, eliminating mosquito breeding sources, and managing the environment. She expressed confidence that policymakers and the scientific community are making concerted efforts in this direction.
The President said that in recent years, dengue has also emerged as a major challenge in the country. This challenge is likely to become even more formidable due to global warming and shifts in monsoon patterns. Research and studies conducted by the ICMR have provided direction to our fight against diseases such as tuberculosis, leprosy, and kala-azar. The ICMR has also played a significant role in shaping our national health programs. During the COVID-19 pandemic, it established a nationwide testing network in record time and partnered in the development of India’s first indigenous COVID-19 vaccine. She expressed confidence that the ICMR is also taking effective measures toward the diagnosis of diseases like dengue.
President said that the occasion of a golden jubilee is not only a time to reflect upon and take pride in past achievements, but also an opportunity to set decisive goals for the future. We are moving forward with the objective of building Viksit Bharat by 2047. Strong collaboration among research institutions, centres of technical and higher education, and the industrial sector is crucial for building a healthy and empowered India. Premier institutions like the ICMR can take the lead in fostering such collaboration. She expressed confidence that the ICMR and its affiliated institutions will contribute to achieving the health-related goals of Viksit Bharat through research, collaboration and innovation.

title: Prime Minister addresses the 21st East Asia Summit in Manila
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                17 NOV 2026 4:13PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi addressed the 21st East Asia Summit (EAS) in Manila, today.
In the current era of crisis and conflicts, PM underscored the need for dialogue, mutual respect and cooperation to support all efforts for peace. Calling for a free, open, inclusive and rules-based Indo-Pacific, Prime Minister stressed that EAS must contribute towards bringing peace, stability and predictability in the global arena.
He particularly highlighted the impact of crisis and conflicts on food, fuel and fertilizer security the world over. He further called for ensuring safety and security of commercial ships and seafarers, who continue to be targeted in international waterways. Prime Minister underlined that India supports all efforts directed at peaceful resolution of the ongoing conflicts in Ukraine and West Asia.
He underscored the threats posed by terrorism to peace loving societies.
To strengthen cooperation across the EAS platform, Prime Minister proposed the following:
I) Seafarers’ Safety Initiative for cooperation in joint training and emergency response.
II) EAS Cyber Crime conference at National Forensic Science University to address new age threats from cross-border crimes such as online frauds and cybercrimes.
III) EAS Maritime Heritage Festival in Lothal.
IV) EAS University Conclave in Nalanda to foster greater academic cooperation with EAS countries.
Prime Minister congratulated the President of the Republic of the Philippines, H.E. Ferdinand R. Marcos for successfully organizing the Summit.

title: English Translation of Prime Minister’s Statement during the 21st East Asia Summit
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                17 NOV 2026 4:10PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Your Excellency, President Marcos,
Your Majesty,
Excellencies,
Namaskar!
I warmly congratulate President Marcos for the excellent organisation of the East Asia Summit.
Friends,
Since the COVID pandemic, the world has been facing one crisis after another. Conflicts are putting increasing pressure on food, fuel, and fertiliser supplies.
Ships and seafarers are also being targeted on international waterways. Alongside the serious threat of terrorism, new forms of cross-border crime, such as cyber fraud and online scams, are also on the rise.
Friends,
Today, what the world needs most is peace, stability, and predictability.
For many years, the East Asia Summit has served as an important platform for finding solutions to shared challenges and strengthening mutual cooperation. This very spirit of dialogue, mutual respect, and cooperation is the cornerstone of India’s foreign policy.
ASEAN unity and centrality are at the heart of our Act East Policy. We are committed to a Free, Open, Inclusive, and Rules-based Indo-Pacific. Whether it is Ukraine or West Asia, we will continue to support every effort towards peace.
Friends,
Our seas are the lifelines of our shared prosperity. Ensuring their security and freedom of navigation is the responsibility of us all.
In this direction, we are launching a Seafarers' Safety Initiative, under which we will enhance cooperation in joint training and emergency response.
Friends,
Ensuring trust and security in the digital world is equally essential. At the AI Impact Summit held in India this year, we emphasized the development of human-centric, inclusive, and safe AI. We also emphasized the need for technologies such as digital watermarking to combat deepfakes and misinformation.
We welcome the Joint Statement issued today on combating online scams.
To effectively address this growing threat, we propose hosting the East Asia Summit Cyber Crime Conference at India’s National Forensic Sciences University.
Friends,
The foundation of our relationship lies in a shared heritage that goes back thousands of years. The National Maritime Heritage Complex, being developed at Lothal in India, will soon showcase this shared heritage to the world. To further strengthen our historical and cultural ties, we will also host the East Asia Summit Maritime Heritage Festival at Lothal.
Next year, we will host the East Asia Summit University Heads Conclave at Nalanda, which will provide fresh impetus to our cooperation in the fields of education and research.
Friends,
This year, we are commemorating the 50th anniversary of the historic Treaty of Amity and Cooperation in Southeast Asia.
Fifty years ago, this region gave the world an important message, the message of peace, respect for sovereignty, and dialogue. Today, that message has become even more relevant. Our shared future will be shaped not by conflict, but by mutual respect and cooperation.
With this vision, India will continue to stand shoulder to shoulder with ASEAN, remaining committed to regional peace, stability, and shared prosperity.
Thank you very much.

title: WOMEN’S REPRESENTATION MUST EXTEND FROM PANCHAYATS TO PARLIAMENT; HOPEFUL OF IMPLEMENTATION OF NARI SHAKTI VANDAN ADHINIYAM: LOK SABHA SPEAKER
subtitle:
WOMEN’S GREATER PARTICIPATION IN POLICYMAKING AND LEGISLATION WILL MAKE DEMOCRACY MORE RESPONSIVE AND ACCOUNTABLE: LOK SABHA SPEAKER

AI AND TECHNOLOGY CAN STRENGTHEN TRANSPARENCY, ACCOUNTABILITY AND EFFECTIVENESS OF DEMOCRATIC INSTITUTIONS: LOK SABHA SPEAKER

INSTITUTIONAL FRAMEWORK TO BE DEVELOPED FOR DIGITAL EMPOWERMENT AND CAPACITY-BUILDING OF WOMEN REPRESENTATIVES: LOK SABHA SPEAKER

LOK SABHA SPEAKER INAUGURATES THE FIRST COMMONWEALTH WOMEN PARLIAMENTARIANS (CWP) INDIA REGION CONFERENCE IN BENGALURU; CM, KARNATAKA AND OTHER DIGNITARIES GRACE THE OCCASION
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                17 NOV 2026 3:32PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Lok Sabha Speaker Shri Om Birla today emphasized the need for greater representation of women across all democratic institutions. Shri Birla noted that women must have an effective role not merely as participants but also in leadership, policymaking and law-making. Referring to the Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam enacted in 2023, he expressed hope that the provision for 33 per cent representation of women in the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies would move towards implementation, enabling women's leadership to extend from Panchayats to Parliament. He noted that several States have already provided for 50 per cent representation of women in Panchayats and Municipalities. Greater participation of women in legislative institutions and decision-making processes would contribute to building a stronger, more sensitive and accountable democracy. Women bring sensitivity, commitment and a strong sense of responsibility to public life, qualities that are particularly important in addressing the aspirations and challenges of society. Highlighting the pivotal role of women in strengthening democratic institutions, Shri Birla mentioned that greater participation of women in policymaking, legislation and decision-making would make democracy more responsive, inclusive and accountable. Shri Birla made these observations while inaugurating the First Commonwealth Women Parliamentarians (CWP) India Region Conference at Bengaluru.
Noting that Artificial Intelligence (AI) and technology are transforming every sphere of social life and, when used responsibly and accountably, he observed that AI can bring significant improvements in governance. He emphasised that public representatives must leverage technology and e-governance to strengthen their engagement with citizens, understand their problems and ensure timely and effective solutions. Technology can play a vital role in establishing transparent, accountable and efficient systems of governance. Observing that Parliamentary Committees function as ‘Mini Parliaments’, the Speaker said that these committees have made valuable contributions towards addressing the socio-economic challenges faced by women and have made important recommendations to the Government. AI and technology can further strengthen their monitoring and oversight functions and make their work more effective. He indicated that a dedicated session on AI and technology would be organised to enhance the understanding and capacities of women Members of Parliament and legislators in this regard.
The Speaker called for the need to develop an institutional framework to strengthen the capacities of elected women representatives across Panchayats, Municipalities, State Legislative Assemblies and Parliament. The initiative should focus on enabling women representatives, including Panchayat Sarpanches and Municipal Chairpersons, to effectively use AI, technology and digital platforms for public engagement, monitoring and ensuring transparency in governance, he noted. Shri Birla stressed that the ability of public representatives to use technology effectively would directly influence the quality of outcomes delivered to citizens, particularly women and people at the grassroots level. He also underscored the importance of mentorship by experienced women legislators to guide emerging leaders and strengthen their legislative and leadership capabilities.
Shri Birla opined that women have made significant contributions to India's journey from the freedom struggle to nation-building and are today providing leadership in virtually every sphere, including education, science, technology, research, entrepreneurship, sports, defence, space and politics. He said that technology and digital platforms are creating new opportunities for women's economic self-reliance and expanding their participation in social and political life. At the same time, empowering women digitally and ensuring a safe digital environment remain important priorities. Highlighting Karnataka's rich democratic heritage, the Speaker referred to the twelfth-century Anubhava Mantapa of Lord Basaveshwara as an important symbol of the region's democratic traditions. He also recalled the courage and valour of Kittur Rani Chennamma, whose legacy continues to inspire generations.
Shri Birla hoped that the two-day conference would provide an important platform for women parliamentarians and legislators from Commonwealth countries to exchange experiences, innovations and best practices. He observed that dialogue, discussion and the exchange of diverse perspectives, including agreement and disagreement, constitute the strength of democracy. Sharing successful practices from different legislatures would help strengthen democratic institutions and promote innovation from Panchayats to Parliament. Expressing confidence in the outcomes of the conference, the Speaker said that women's leadership would help take the nation towards a more inclusive, balanced and just society, with democratic institutions becoming stronger, more accountable and result-oriented, ensuring that the voice of the last person in society is heard and addressed.
Earlier, the Speaker welcomed the participants and thanked Dr. D. Purandeswari, Chairperson of the Commonwealth Women Parliamentarians Conference in India, the Chief Minister of Karnataka and the Presiding Officers of the Karnataka Legislative Assembly and Legislative Council for their initiative and efforts in organising the conference.
AS INDIA MOVES TOWARDS THE VISION OF VIKSIT BHARAT BY 2047, THE ROLE OF WOMEN IN SHAPING THE NATION'S FUTURE: SMT. D. PURANDESWARI
Addressing the gathering, Chairperson, CWP India Region, Dr. Daggubati Purandeswari noted that women's empowerment in a democracy cannot be measured only by the number of women occupying public offices. It must also be reflected in their ability to participate meaningfully in legislative debates, influence policy decisions, exercise leadership and contribute to the governance and development of the nation. She stressed that we must move beyond ensuring representation towards creating an enabling environment in which women can exercise their leadership with much aplomb and effectiveness. Appreciating Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam, 2023, she said that the legislation represents a historic step towards strengthening women's political representation. Greater participation of women in legislatures will bring wider perspectives, experiences and concerns into public policy and democratic deliberations, she added.
Speaking on the Theme of the Conference, the Chairperson of the CWP India Region observed that the outcome of the discussions in the Conference should not remain confined to resolutions and recommendations. We must strive to develop an actionable framework for strengthening gender-sensitive parliamentary institutions and enhancing the leadership capabilities of women public representatives, she suggested. She further noted that as India moves towards the vision of Viksit Bharat by 2047, the role of women in shaping the nation's future will be decisive and a developed India cannot be realised without the equal participation, leadership and contribution of its women.
Chief Minister, Karnataka, Shri D. K. Shivakumar delivered the Keynote Address. Deputy Chairman, Rajya Sabha, Shri Harivansh; Deputy Chief Minister, Karnataka, Dr. G. Parameshwara; and Speaker, Speaker, Karnataka Legislative Assembly, Shri G. S. Patil also addressed the gathering on this occasion. Chairman, Karnataka Legislative Council, Shri Saleem Ahmed delivered the Welcome Address and Deputy Chairman, Karnataka legislative Council, Dr. Umashree delivered the Vote of Thanks.
135 women law makers from Parliament of India and State Legislatures are participating in the two - day Conference. Theme of the Conference is ‘Strong Foundations, Stronger Voices: Inclusive Cyberspace and Mentorship Pathways for New Women Legislators’. Two Plenary Sessions will be held during the Conference: (i) ‘Empowering Women Digitally: Safe Cyberspace, Smart Choices’, and (ii)  ‘Capacity Building and Mentorship for Women Legislators’, In a special initiative complementing the broader deliberations, UN Women India will organise a side event on Menopause on 17 November 2026. The Conference will conclude on 18 November 2026 with the Valedictory Address of Governor, Karnataka, Dr. Sudha Yadav.
The Conference is expected to achieve the following outcomes:
Facilitate the exchange of experiences, perspectives and good practices on creating safe and inclusive cyber space and digital empowerment for women legislators.
Identify effective frameworks to mentorship, capacity building and leadership development, particularly for newly elected women legislators.
Explore the ways to strengthen institutional safeguards and mechanisms to ensure meaningful participation of women in parliamentary processes.
Promote cooperation and collaboration among legislatures in advancing women's parliamentary leadership.
बेंगलुरु के विधान सौध में आयोजित First Commonwealth Women Parliamentarians Conference के उद्घाटन सत्र को संबोधित किया। 
इस अवसर पर Commonwealth Countries की महिला सांसदों एवं विभिन्न राज्यों एवं केंद्र शासित प्रदेशों से आए विधायकों और जनप्रतिनिधियों के साथ महिला नेतृत्व और लोकतांत्रिक संस्थाओं में उनकी प्रभावी भागीदारी पर विचार साझा किए।

भगवान बसवेश्वर के ‘अनुभव मंडपम’ की गौरवशाली लोकतांत्रिक परंपरा और कित्तूर की रानी चेन्नम्मा के अदम्य शौर्य की साक्षी कर्नाटक की यह धरती ज्ञान, नवाचार और प्रगतिशील चेतना की विशिष्ट पहचान रखती है। भारत के स्वतंत्रता संग्राम, संविधान निर्माण और राष्ट्र के नवनिर्माण में महिलाओं का योगदान अविस्मरणीय रहा है। आज वे शिक्षा, विज्ञान, प्रौद्योगिकी, खेल, अंतरिक्ष, रक्षा और राजनीति सहित प्रत्येक क्षेत्र में अपनी प्रतिभा एवं नेतृत्व से नए प्रतिमान स्थापित कर रही हैं।

वर्तमान समय में AI और डिजिटल माध्यमों का उत्तरदायी एवं नैतिक उपयोग नीति निर्माण, विधायी कार्यवाही, जनसंवाद और सुशासन को अधिक प्रभावी बना सकता है। ऐसे में, technology और AI के इस युग में महिलाओं का Digital Empowerment तथा उनके लिए सुरक्षित Cyber Space सुनिश्चित करना हमारी सामूहिक जिम्मेदारी है।

title: 9th Naturopathy Day to Be Observed Across India on 18 November
subtitle:
‘Prakritik Chikitsa, Swasth Bharat’ to be the Theme of This Year’s Observance

National Programme to Be Held at the Central Research Institute of Yoga and Naturopathy, Nagamangala, Karnataka

Focus on Preventive Healthcare, Obesity Prevention and Lifestyle-Related Disorders
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                17 NOV 2026 3:36PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Ministry of Ayush will observe the 9th Naturopathy Day on 18 November 2026 at the Central Research Institute of Yoga and Naturopathy (CRIYN), Nagamangala, Karnataka, under the theme ‘Prakritik Chikitsa, Swasth Bharat’. The observance will highlight the role of naturopathy in promoting preventive healthcare, healthy lifestyles and overall well-being, with a special focus on addressing obesity and lifestyle-related disorders.
To mark the importance of the day, the inaugural session of the main event at Nagamangala will see many initiatives of importance and of wider reach. Among the key highlights will be a dedicated community health initiative alongside several other impactful programmes that will serve as the main attraction of the event, aiming to foster holistic well-being and sustainable community development. These programs are thoughtfully designed to engage participants from all walks of life and create lasting positive change across the region. Together, they underscore a strong commitment to public welfare and inclusive progress.
This year's theme underscores the importance of adopting healthier lifestyles through appropriate dietary practices, physical activity, yoga, stress management, and other evidence-informed naturopathic approaches contributing to a healthier India. It seeks to strengthen public awareness about the importance of prevention and encourage individuals and communities to take an active role in maintaining their health and well-being. The observance also aligns with the Prime Minister's vision for a Fit and Healthy India, emphasising preventive healthcare and healthy living.
As part of the nationwide outreach, the observance will feature ten sub-themes focusing on different sections of society and key areas of public health. These include ‘Mother Nature – Healthy Mother, Healthy Family’, ‘Swastha Mahila – Fit & Healthy Women’, ‘Fit Force – Strong, Lean & Healthy Force’, ‘Healthy Campus – Fit Students, Healthy Nation’, ‘Healthy Workplace – Fit Workforce’ and ‘Safe Journey – Fit Driver, Safe Journey’.
The other sub themes include ‘Golden Wellness – Active Ageing, Healthy Ageing’, ‘Prakriti se Samarth – Healthy & Active Living’, ‘Natural Strength for Sporting Excellence’ and ‘Prakriti Kisan – Fit Farmer, Healthy Nation’. These initiatives seek to extend the message of naturopathy to families, women, students, working professionals, armed forces personnel, senior citizens, sportspersons and farmers, encouraging healthier practices across communities.
The observance will also highlight the efforts of the Ministry of Ayush towards strengthening the institutional, research and healthcare infrastructure for yoga and naturopathy in the country. Through its research institutions and initiatives, the Ministry is working to advance scientific research, education and the wider integration of naturopathy in preventive and promotive healthcare.
The 9th Naturopathy Day will serve as a platform to strengthen public engagement with naturopathy and reinforce the importance of healthy lifestyles, preventive healthcare and community participation in building a Swasth Bharat.

title: Union Agriculture Minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan visits Samrala, Punjab, under ‘Khet Bachao Abhiyan’; says “farmers’ plans will be made in the fields, not sitting in offices in Delhi”
subtitle:
Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan gives a strong message to those who blame farmers for stubble burning: “Farmers are food providers; stubble is food for the soil and a means of increasing organic carbon”

Integrated farming can transform farmers’ livelihoods: “Punjab Agricultural University’s three-crop model can generate savings of up to ₹1.5 lakh per acre,” says Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan, praising the initiative

Government takes strict action against black marketing of fertilisers and fake pesticides: “Farmer IDs will prevent the diversion of urea and DAP; stringent legislation to be introduced against counterfeit pesticides,” says Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan

Major relief for potato, onion and tomato growers: “Central government to bear the entire transportation cost when farmers sell their produce in other states,” says Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan

Government to intervene directly when prices of fruits and vegetables fall: “Under the Market Intervention Scheme, compensation for losses will be transferred directly to farmers’ bank accounts,” says Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan

Focus on mechanisation and natural farming to make small landholdings profitable: Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan assures farmers that machinery for stubble management will be made more affordable
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                17 NOV 2026 9:29PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Minister for Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare, and Rural Development, Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan today interacted directly with farmers and agricultural scientists at a programme organised at Krishi Vigyan Kendra (KVK), Samrala, in Ludhiana, Punjab, under the nationwide ‘Khet Bachao Abhiyan’, being conducted from 22 October to 30 November 2026 with the resolve of ‘Healthy Soil, Prosperous Farmers’. Paying tribute to the land of Punjab and acknowledging the innovations developed by Punjab Agricultural University (PAU), the Union Minister discussed several important aspects of agricultural development, including integrated farming, crop diversification, soil health and stubble management. He also outlined key initiatives and forthcoming measures by the central government to help farmers obtain fair prices for their produce. Emphasising the need to make agriculture more sustainable and profitable, he said that policies and programmes must be shaped by understanding the actual needs of farmers and the challenges they face in their fields. The interaction focused on practical ways to improve farm incomes, make better use of available resources and protect the long-term health of agricultural land.
At the beginning of the programme, Union Minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan paid his respects to Shri Guru Nanak Dev Ji and said that the path shown by Guru Sahib through the teachings of ‘Kirat Karo, Naam Japo and Vand Chhako’ – “work honestly, remember the divine and share with others” – had the power to make the entire world a better place. He said that he had not come to the programme with the arrogance of a ministerial position, but as a farmer and as ‘Mama’, to serve the farming community. Shri Chouhan emphasised that agricultural policies and schemes should not be formulated by sitting in closed rooms in Delhi. Instead, those responsible for making decisions must go to the fields, sit with farmers and understand their experiences, requirements and difficulties first-hand. He said that farmers should be at the centre of agricultural policymaking, and that their voices and practical knowledge must guide decisions that affect their livelihoods. According to him, meaningful agricultural planning can only emerge through direct engagement with those who work on the land.
Saluting the hard work and contribution of Punjab’s farmers, Shri Chouhan recalled that there was a time when India was compelled to import red wheat from other countries to meet its food requirements. However, following the Green Revolution, which began in Punjab, the country’s foodgrain reserves had grown substantially, and India was now in a position to meet its food requirements with its own production. He said that India had overtaken China to become the world’s largest producer of rice and was the second-largest producer of wheat. He credited the farmers of Punjab for playing a major role in this transformation and for helping strengthen the country’s food security through their dedication and hard work. Referring to Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s visit to Manila, he also mentioned that the Prime Minister had paid obeisance at the Khalsa Diwan Gurdwara there and laid the foundation stone for its reconstruction along with members of the sangat. Shri Chouhan said that such gestures reflected the importance of the Sikh community's traditions and its contribution to society.
Expressing concern over the declining size of agricultural landholdings, Union Minister Shri Chouhan said that India did not have the kind of large farms, extending over thousands of hectares, that were common in some other countries. It was therefore essential to develop farming models that could generate higher returns from smaller areas of land. He praised the three-crop model developed by Punjab Agricultural University, under which farmers could cultivate three crops on just one acre and earn a net annual income of up to ₹1.5 lakh. He described the model as an important example of how small landholdings could be used more productively and profitably. He also instructed KVK Samrala to take steps to popularise the model across the region so that more farmers could learn about it and adopt it according to their own requirements. He said that such practical models could help address the challenges arising from shrinking landholdings while improving the economic prospects of small farmers.
Shri Chouhan said that continued dependence on the wheat-paddy cropping cycle was gradually reducing the fertility of agricultural land. He urged farmers to diversify their crops and move towards integrated farming by combining foodgrain cultivation with activities such as growing fruits, flowers and vegetables, cultivating medicinal plants, animal husbandry, goat rearing and fish farming. He explained that farmers should not rely exclusively on wheat and paddy, but should explore other suitable agricultural and allied activities based on their land, resources and local conditions. By combining different crops and activities, farmers could make better use of their land, create additional sources of income and reduce their dependence on a single cropping pattern. He stressed that crop diversification and integrated farming were important not only for improving farmers’ earnings but also for maintaining the long-term productivity and health of the soil.
Addressing the deteriorating condition of soil and the indiscriminate use of fertilisers, Shri Chouhan said that applying excessive quantities of fertilisers and pesticides without first testing the soil was harming the natural ecosystem of agricultural land. Such practices were destroying beneficial insects and earthworms, which play an important role in maintaining soil fertility. He appealed to farmers to experiment with natural farming on at least half of their land rather than attempting to shift their entire holdings to the practice immediately. He said that adopting natural farming on a portion of their land would help improve soil health and that farmers would be able to maintain their production levels as well. He encouraged them to assess the results and gradually expand the practice. He emphasised that farmers needed to pay greater attention to the actual nutritional requirements of their soil and avoid unnecessary use of chemical inputs. Protecting soil health, he said, was essential for sustaining agricultural productivity and ensuring that farmland remained fertile for future generations.
Taking a clear stand in support of farmers on the issue of stubble burning, Shri Chouhan said that farmers should not be unfairly blamed or portrayed negatively every time the issue of pollution was discussed. He said that farmers were becoming increasingly aware of the importance of managing crop residue and were making efforts to handle stubble rather than burn it. Stubble, he emphasised, was food for the soil, and incorporating it into the field helped increase organic carbon content. It therefore had an important role to play in maintaining soil health and improving the quality of agricultural land. He assured farmers that the government would work towards making machinery such as seeders, used for stubble management, more affordable and ensuring that mechanisation schemes were better suited to their needs. He said that farmers needed access to practical and cost-effective equipment to manage crop residue without resorting to burning. The government, he added, would focus on making such machinery more accessible and helping farmers adopt suitable mechanised solutions.
Tak marketing, Shri Chouhan said that the central government was making DAP available to farmers at ₹1,350 per bag, even though its cost was approximately ₹5,000. Similarly, a bag of urea costing around ₹3,000 was being supplied to farmers at just ₹266. He explained that the government was bearing the substantial subsidy burden to ensure that farmers could obtain these essential inputs at affordable prices. To prevent subsidised fertilisers from being diverted for industrial purposes or other unauthorised uses, the government was rapidly issuing ‘Farmer IDs’. He informed farmers that six lakh Farmer IDs had already been created in Punjab. These IDs would help ensure that fertilisers reached the farmers who needed them, in a timely manner and in quantities based on the actual requirements of their land and crops, including crops such as potatoes. He said that the system would help prevent the diversion and misuse of subsidised urea and DAP. He also announced that the central government was preparing to introduce a new and stringent Pesticide Act, along with a new seed law, to protect farmers from fake pesticides and poor-quality seeds being sold in the market. The proposed legal measures would strengthen safeguards against fraudulent and substandard agricultural inputs.
Referring to fluctuations in crop prices and the need to eliminate the role of middlemen, Union Minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan outlined two major measures to provide relief to farmers. He said that if prices of potatoes, onions or tomatoes fell in Punjab, while better prices were available in major cities such as Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata or Chennai, the central government would bear the entire transportation cost of moving the produce to those markets for sale through state government agencies. This would allow farmers to access better-paying markets in other states without having to bear the additional burden of transportation expenses. He also explained that under the ‘Market Intervention Scheme’, if farmers were compelled to sell their produce at very low prices, the central and state governments would intervene jointly, sharing the cost equally, with each contributing 50 per cent. The amount representing the difference in prices would then be transferred directly to the farmers’ bank accounts. These measures, he said, were intended to protect farmers against sharp price declines, reduce the impact of market fluctuations and ensure that they received better returns for their produce.
During the programme, Shri Chouhan also appreciated the use of a modern, driverless, mapping-based tractor, recognising the potential of such technology in agricultural operations. He said that agriculture was a state subject, but there should be no politics between the central and state governments when it came to serving farmers and addressing their concerns. He informed the gathering that the central government had approved all the proposals submitted by Punjab’s Agriculture Minister under the Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana (RKVY). He reiterated that the Centre was ready to work with the state government to support agricultural development and improve the welfare of farmers. Shri Chouhan also said that any farmer wishing to share suggestions or raise concerns could meet him directly in Delhi by arranging an appointment. He stressed that farmers should feel free to bring their problems and ideas to his attention so that their concerns could be considered and addressed. Union Agriculture Commissioner P.K. Singh, PAU Vice-Chancellor Dr Harvinder Singh Dhaliwal, and a large number of agricultural scientists and progressive farmers were present on the occasion.

date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                17 NOV 2026 7:42PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Minister for Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare, and Rural Development, Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan today participated in the ‘Khet Bachao Abhiyan’ programme organised at Badarpur village in Sahibzada Ajit Singh Nagar district (Mohali), Punjab, and announced significant support for the state’s farmers. In the presence of Punjab Agriculture Minister Shri Gurmeet Singh Khuddian, Shri Chouhan handed over an approval letter for the release of ₹254.20 crore as the second tranche of the Mother Sanction under the Pradhan Mantri Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana (PM-RKVY) for the financial year 2026–27. In addition, the central government approved seven new agricultural projects under the state’s Annual Action Plan, with a total outlay of ₹98.44 crore. Addressing the programme, the Union Minister announced strict action against those involved in the black marketing of fertilisers and the practice of forcibly tagging other products with fertiliser purchases. He said that those found engaging in such practices would face imprisonment. He also announced that a stringent new pesticide law would be introduced to curb the sale of fake pesticides and other substandard agricultural inputs. Alongside these measures, he shared details of a new green ammonia trial across 10,000 hectares, being undertaken as an alternative to urea.
Paying his respects to Punjab, the sacred land of Guru Nanak Dev Ji, Union Agriculture Minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan said that the soldiers of Punjab had always stood firm in defending the nation, while the state’s farmers had filled the country’s granaries through their hard work and contribution to the Green Revolution. Recalling that Guru Nanak Dev Ji’s Prakash Parv (birth anniversary) would be celebrated on the coming 24th , Shri Chouhan said that the teachings of Guru Sahib, particularly the message of ‘Kirat Karo, Naam Japo and Vand Chhako’ – “work honestly, remember the divine and share with others” – continued to inspire humanity towards service, hard work and dedication. These values, he said, offered renewed motivation and energy for serving society. Speaking emotionally to the farmers gathered there, he said, “My farmer brothers and sisters, I am a ‘Mama’ to you before I am a minister. For me, serving farmers is no less than worshipping God.” He emphasised that the welfare of farmers was a responsibility that went beyond official positions and political considerations.
Centre and state will work together to serve farmers: ₹254.20 crore in support for Punjab
Reaffirming his commitment to farmers’ welfare above political differences, Union Minister Shri Shivraj Chouhan said that the central and state governments might be run by different political parties, but that should make no difference to their shared responsibility towards farmers. Their sole objective, he stressed, must be to improve the lives and livelihoods of Punjab’s farmers. In keeping with this commitment, he handed over the approval letter for ₹254.20 crore under PM-RKVY to Punjab Agriculture Minister Shri Gurmeet Singh Khuddian. In addition to this allocation, the central government had also approved seven new projects worth ₹98.44 crore in response to the Punjab government’s request. These projects, included in the state’s Annual Action Plan, are intended to support agricultural development across Punjab. The approved funds will help increase agricultural productivity, strengthen modern agricultural infrastructure and give fresh momentum to the overall development of the state’s agriculture sector. Shri Chouhan said that the Centre was committed to extending the necessary support to states for the benefit of farmers, irrespective of political differences between governments.
Strict warning against fertiliser tagging and black marketing; new Pesticide Act to be introduced
Taking a firm stand on issues affecting farmers, Union Minister Shri Chouhan made it clear that no dealer or shopkeeper would be permitted to force farmers to purchase unnecessary products along with fertilisers through the practice of ‘tagging’. He said that, under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, the central government imported fertilisers at high international prices and provided them to farmers with substantial subsidies so that farmers could access essential agricultural inputs at affordable rates and benefit from their use. Anyone found indulging in black marketing or forcibly tagging other products with fertilisers, he warned, would face strict action. “If anyone engages in black marketing or tagging, the only place for them will be jail,” he said. He also announced that the government was preparing to replace the existing Pesticide Act with a new and much stricter law to tackle the problem of fake fertilisers, spurious seeds and substandard pesticides at its root. The proposed legislation is intended to strengthen safeguards for farmers against poor-quality and fraudulent agricultural inputs. Suggestions are being sought from farmers and experts across the country as part of the process of framing the new law. Shri Chouhan said that the government was determined to take firm measures to protect farmers from practices that increase their costs and compromise agricultural productivity.
Green ammonia trial across 10,000 hectares; call to protect soil health
Union Minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan said that he believed in sitting with farmers on the boundaries of their fields and understanding their concerns while shaping policies, rather than making decisions while remaining confined to an office in Delhi. During the programme, he witnessed a live demonstration of green ammonia and informed farmers that the government was undertaking a trial of this technology across 10,000 hectares for the first time, with green ammonia being explored as an alternative to urea. If successful, the initiative could bring substantial benefits to farmers. Highlighting the need to protect soil health, he said that just as excessive consumption of medicines makes a person ill, indiscriminate use of urea, DAP and other chemical fertilisers was making ‘Mother Earth’ sick. He urged farmers to get their soil tested before applying fertilisers and nutrients, and to use only those nutrients, and only in the quantities that their fields actually required. This would help maintain soil fertility while avoiding unnecessary expenditure and excessive chemical use. The Minister also appreciated farmer Bhupinder Singh Ji for managing crop residue by incorporating stubble into the soil instead of burning it. Praising Punjab’s efforts to bring down incidents of stubble burning continuously, he said that the state was increasingly setting an example for the rest of the country. He urged farmers to continue adopting responsible crop-residue management practices to protect the environment and preserve the health of their soil.
Major decisions on crop diversification, integrated farming and the Honey Board
Shri Chouhan said that continued dependence on the wheat-paddy cropping cycle alone was neither beneficial for soil health nor adequate for improving farmers’ incomes in the long run. He encouraged small farmers to adopt integrated farming, explaining that combining crop cultivation with activities such as fruit and vegetable production, animal husbandry, fisheries, poultry, goat rearing, mushroom cultivation and beekeeping could provide a regular source of income throughout the year. By diversifying their activities and making better use of available land and resources, farmers could reduce their dependence on a single crop and create additional income opportunities. He said that the government aimed to bring more integrated farming projects to farmers through the next Budget as well, under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi. The objective would be to promote crop diversification and integrated farming in a manner that particularly benefits small farmers and makes their livelihoods more secure.
During his interaction with farmers, Union Minister Shri Chouhan appreciated the innovative efforts of progressive farmers Jagdish Ji, who is engaged in organic farming, Sahiwal dairy farming and beekeeping; Fateh Singh Ji, who sells pure milk and sweets directly to consumers without involving middlemen; and Ratanjot Ji, who has established a vermicompost project on five acres. Describing progressive farmers such as these as role models for the country, Shri Chouhan praised their efforts to develop practical and sustainable models of agricultural enterprise. He directed that a special meeting of the National Beekeeping Board (Honey Board) be convened to discuss and address the problems faced by honey producers. He also called for the certification process for organic products to be simplified so that farmers producing organic goods could access certification more easily. In addition, farmers raised several local concerns, including the demand for an 80 per cent subsidy on agricultural machinery for small groups, the modernisation of Morinda Sugar Mill and the problem of stray cattle. Shri Chouhan assured them that positive steps would be taken in coordination with the state government to address these issues. He said that the concerns raised directly by farmers would be taken up with the relevant authorities so that practical solutions could be explored.
Punjab Agriculture Minister Shri Gurmeet Singh Khuddian, senior leader Shri Sunil Jakhar, the Vice-Chancellor of the Agricultural University, senior agriculture department officials from the central and state governments, scientists from Krishi Vigyan Kendras (KVKs), and a large number of progressive farmers and representatives of farmer organisations were present on the occasion.

content:
The Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) and the Research and Information System for Developing Countries (RIS) signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) on 17 November 2026 at New Delhi to strengthen agricultural cooperation and knowledge exchange across countries of the Global South. The MoU was exchanged by Dr M. L. Jat, Secretary, Department of Agricultural Research and Education (DARE) and Director General, ICAR, and Prof. Sachin Kumar Sharma, Director General, RIS. The partnership, facilitated through DAKSHIN – Global South Centre of Excellence, will focus on sharing agricultural technologies, documenting best practices, knowledge exchange and capacity-building.
Speaking at the inaugural session of the High-Level Policy Dialogue on “Global South: Towards a New Strategic Partnership”, Shri Kirti Vardhan Singh, Minister of State for External Affairs, Government of India, emphasised that the Global South must strengthen its collective voice in shaping global narratives, building economic resilience and ensuring equitable access to emerging technologies, particularly Artificial Intelligence. He called for stronger India–Africa partnerships, greater institutional collaboration and active engagement of young researchers and policymakers in translating knowledge into meaningful policy outcomes.
Recalling the vision of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi at the Second Voice of the Global South Summit in November 2023, the Minister highlighted the importance of developing common perspectives on shared challenges, strengthening economic resilience and promoting affordable, scalable and locally relevant development solutions. He emphasised the need to move beyond traditional development cooperation towards co-development and shared solutions.
Dr M. L. Jat, Secretary, DARE and Director General, ICAR, highlighted ICAR's role as a century-old apex organisation for agricultural research, education and extension, with 114 research institutions, 152 regional research centres and 731 Krishi Vigyan Kendras (KVKs), while coordinating with nearly 80 agricultural universities. He informed that ICAR has 74 Memoranda of Understanding with different countries and institutions, of which nearly 60 per cent are with institutions from the Global South.
Dr Jat emphasised that the partnership with RIS and DAKSHIN would further strengthen South–South collaboration by facilitating the exchange and application of available agricultural technologies, practices, systems, methods and tools across countries. He also highlighted the importance of identifying suitable agro-climatic and research domains to connect countries. He mentioned the proposed Science and Partnership Week in mid-April 2027, which will bring together participants from the Global South and North in India, and the idea of convening Global South and North leaders to discuss their respective needs and available capabilities through demand-driven partnerships.
Prof. Sachin Kumar Sharma, Director General, RIS, highlighted the importance of agriculture for the Global South and the need for knowledge sharing, mutual learning and cooperation. Drawing upon his experience in agricultural negotiations at the World Trade Organization (WTO), he highlighted the need to strengthen the voice and concerns of Global South countries in multilateral negotiations and global decision-making. He noted that RIS has a strong network across the Global South, while ICAR brings extensive agricultural technologies, research and best practices. He emphasised that the partnership would facilitate the sharing of Indian technologies and practices with other countries, particularly those with similar agro-climatic conditions, while also enabling mutual learning from partner countries.
H.E. Prof. Anil Sooklal, High Commissioner of South Africa to India, described the present global uncertainty as a defining moment for the Global South to assert its leadership in shaping a multipolar world order. He called for reforms in global governance, stronger strategic partnerships and the generation of knowledge and policy perspectives from within the Global South.
H.E. Mr Alem Tsehaye Woldemariam, Ambassador of the State of Eritrea to India and Dean of the Diplomatic Corps in India, emphasised the importance of translating the historical solidarity between India and Africa into meaningful partnerships through economic cooperation, connectivity, infrastructure development and youth engagement.
Ms Archna Vyas, Country Director, Gates Foundation, India, identified Digital Public Infrastructure, health security, agriculture and food systems, Artificial Intelligence and institutional capacity-building as promising areas for India–Africa cooperation. She stressed that effective partnerships must be grounded in country ownership, co-creation and mutual learning, with a focus on affordable and scalable solutions.
Dr Rajan Sudesh Ratna, Coordinator, DAKSHIN – Global South Centre of Excellence, reaffirmed DAKSHIN's commitment to moving from dialogue to actionable partnerships through country-led priorities, institutional cooperation and capacity-building.
The MoU signing took place during the two-day High-Level Policy Dialogue organised by RIS–DAKSHIN in partnership with the Ministry of External Affairs, Government of India, on 17–18 November 2026 at the India Habitat Centre, New Delhi, on the occasion of DAKSHIN Day 2026. The dialogue brings together diplomats, policymakers, researchers, development practitioners and representatives of academic and partner institutions to deliberate on strengthening South–South cooperation, with particular emphasis on the evolving India–Africa strategic partnership. The collaboration between ICAR and RIS aims to promote the exchange of agricultural technologies, knowledge, best practices and capacity-building opportunities across the Global South.

title: India’s Horticulture Production Set to Reach Record 386.9 Million Tonnes in 2025-26: Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan Releases Third Advance Estimates
subtitle:
Horticulture production estimated to rise by 4.36% despite a decline in cultivated area; fruits, vegetables, flowers and plantation crops register strong growth

Potato production projected to increase by nearly 12%; overall horticulture output expected to grow by 16.17 million tonnes

Diversification into fruits, vegetables, spices and high-value crops creating new opportunities for farmers: Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                17 NOV 2026 12:25PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Minister for Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare and Rural Development, Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan, today released the Third Advance Estimates of area and production of horticultural crops for 2025-26, bringing encouraging news for the country's farmers. According to the latest estimates, India's total horticulture production is expected to reach 3,869.15 lakh tonnes in 2025-26, an increase of 161.77 lakh tonnes, or 4.36%, over the 3,707.38 lakh tonnes recorded in 2024-25. Expressing satisfaction over the projected growth, Shri Chouhan said the significant increase in horticulture production reflects the hard work of India's farmers and the impact of the farmer-friendly policies of the government under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi. The Minister said that this record production would not only strengthen the country's nutritional security but also directly contribute to higher incomes for horticulture farmers. He congratulated farmers across the country for their efforts and said the growth reflects the dedication and hard work of India's farming community.
Shri Chouhan observed that Indian agriculture is witnessing significant and encouraging diversification, with farmers increasingly moving beyond traditional crops towards the cultivation of fruits, vegetables, flowers, spices, plantation crops such as cashew, coconut and cocoa, as well as aromatic and medicinal plants. This growing interest in commercial and high-value crops is opening up new avenues of income for farmers while creating fresh opportunities for self-reliance and growth in the agricultural sector. According to the Minister, one of the most significant aspects of the latest estimates is the increase in production despite a reduction in the area under horticulture. The total area under horticultural crops in 2025-26 is estimated at approximately 297.21 lakh hectares, compared with 301.36 lakh hectares in 2024-25. Despite the decline in cultivated area, production is projected to increase across fruits, vegetables, flowers, plantation crops, and aromatic and medicinal plants.
The estimates, released by the Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare on the basis of information received from States, Union Territories and other government agencies, reflect the sector's continued growth and improved productivity.
Fruit production projected to increase by 4.60%
Fruit production is estimated to rise from 1,176.49 lakh tonnes in 2024-25 to 1,230.66 lakh tonnes in 2025-26, an increase of 54.18 lakh tonnes or 4.60%. The improved output is primarily attributed to better production of banana, mango, papaya, apple, pomegranate and jackfruit.
Vegetable production expected to reach 2,272.68 lakh tonnes
Farmers have also registered encouraging growth in vegetable cultivation. The area under vegetables is estimated to increase from 117.91 lakh hectares to 119.31 lakh hectares. Vegetable production is projected to rise by 4.35%, from 2,177.97 lakh tonnes in 2024-25 to 2,272.68 lakh tonnes in 2025-26. The increase is primarily driven by higher production of potato, tomato, brinjal, bottle gourd, cucumber, cabbage, beans and peas. Potato and tomato production are both expected to register strong growth. Potato production is estimated at 655.70 lakh tonnes, up 11.95% from 585.71 lakh tonnes in the previous year. Tomato production is projected to increase from 205.99 lakh tonnes to 214.11 lakh tonnes. Onion production is estimated at 288.96 lakh tonnes.
Flower production registers nearly 14.5% growth
A significant increase is also expected in flower production. Output is projected to rise by approximately 14.45%, from 42.65 lakh tonnes in 2024-25 to 48.82 lakh tonnes in 2025-26. The area under flower cultivation has also increased to 4.10 lakh hectares.
Plantation crops and medicinal plants record growth
The Third Advance Estimates also indicate an increase in both the area and production of plantation crops, including arecanut, coconut, cashew, betel leaves and cocoa. Their combined production is estimated to increase by 7.56% to 182.64 lakh tonnes. Production of aromatic and medicinal plants is also expected to rise from 9.01 lakh tonnes to 9.28 lakh tonnes.
Spice production estimated at 123.54 lakh tonnes
According to data from the Directorate of Arecanut and Spices Development, improved production of turmeric, garlic, curry leaves and cardamom is expected to support growth in the spices sector. The total area under spices in 2025-26 is estimated at 47.56 lakh hectares, with production projected at 123.54 lakh tonnes.

content:
Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal is on an official visit to the Italian Republic from 17 to 18 November 2026. The visit aims to further strengthen the India–Italy economic partnership, with particular emphasis on expanding bilateral trade, promoting investment, deepening industrial and technological cooperation, and strengthening business-to-business and startup linkages.
India and Italy share a longstanding relationship rooted in historical, civilisational and people-to-people ties, which has evolved into a multifaceted partnership encompassing political, economic, defence, scientific and cultural cooperation. Under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, India–Italy relations have gained renewed momentum, culminating in the elevation of bilateral ties to a Special Strategic Partnership during the Prime Minister’s visit to Italy on 19–20 May 2026. The two countries are implementing the India–Italy Joint Strategic Action Plan 2025–29 and have set a target of increasing annual bilateral trade to €20 billion by 2029.
During the visit, Shri Piyush Goyal will hold a bilateral meeting with H.E. Mr Antonio Tajani, Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation of Italy. He will also co-chair the 23rd Session of the India–Italy Joint Commission for Economic Cooperation (JCEC) and participate in the India–Italy Business and Innovation Forum. In addition, the Minister will meet Chief Executive Officers of leading Italian companies and interact with the Indian business delegation. These engagements are expected to provide further impetus to bilateral trade, investment, industrial cooperation and innovation linkages.
The 23rd Session of the India–Italy JCEC will be co-chaired by Shri Piyush Goyal and H.E. Mr Antonio Tajani on 18 November 2026 at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation in Rome.
The JCEC is the principal institutional mechanism for reviewing and guiding India–Italy economic and commercial cooperation. The 22nd Session, co-chaired by the two Ministers in Brescia in June 2025, prioritised cooperation in Industry 4.0, aerospace, energy transition and sustainable mobility, and agreed to establish Joint Working Groups on automobiles and space. The 23rd Session will provide an opportunity to review progress in bilateral trade and investment relations and discuss measures to further diversify and expand the bilateral trade basket. Discussions will cover automobiles and auto components, industrial machinery, agriculture and food processing, pharmaceuticals and chemicals, renewable energy, aerospace and space, startups and innovation, and connectivity, among other areas of mutual interest.
Italy is India’s fourth-largest trading partner in the European Union. During April–August 2026, India’s exports to Italy grew by 29.9% to USD 3.92 billion over the corresponding period of the previous year. India’s major exports to Italy include iron and steel and metal products, electrical and electronic equipment, chemicals, and textiles and apparel, while its major imports include machinery and electrical equipment, chemicals and metal products.
A high-level Indian business delegation comprising around 80 business leaders and startups from diverse sectors will participate in the India–Italy Business and Innovation Forum in Rome on 18 November 2026. The Forum will feature an interactive session with Italian promotion agencies, namely ICE – Italian Trade Agency, Cassa Depositi e Prestiti (CDP), SACE and SIMEST, business-to-business meetings, and parallel thematic sessions on Automotive and Automotive Components; Industrial and Agri-food Machinery and Food Processing; Pharmaceuticals and Chemicals; and Renewable Energy and Circular Economy.
Shri Piyush Goyal will interact with the business delegation and address the Plenary Session of the Forum along with H.E. Mr Antonio Tajani.
A dedicated Innovation Forum on Startups and Innovators will also be held as part of the Business and Innovation Forum. India is home to the world’s third-largest startup ecosystem, with over 2.61 lakh startups recognised under the Startup India initiative as of 31 October 2026. The Forum will provide Indian startups with an opportunity to engage with Italian investors, research institutions and industry, and explore partnerships, market access and collaboration in emerging technologies.
During the visit, Shri Piyush Goyal will also hold meetings with Chief Executive Officers of leading Italian companies in sectors such as heavy engineering, aviation services and clean energy to discuss investment and partnership opportunities in India. Following the Forum, members of the Indian business delegation will undertake industrial visits in Italy on 19 November 2026.
The visit reflects India’s continued commitment to strengthening its economic engagement with Italy, an important partner in the European Union and a key economy in the Mediterranean region. With the conclusion of negotiations for the India–EU Free Trade Agreement in January 2026, both countries have significant opportunities to expand bilateral trade and investment across sectors, including manufacturing, automobiles, machinery, food processing, pharmaceuticals, chemicals, textiles, renewable energy, aerospace and emerging technologies.
The visit is expected to provide fresh momentum to the India–Italy Special Strategic Partnership, strengthen institutional cooperation and create new opportunities for bilateral trade, investment and industrial collaboration.

title: India’s Electronic Goods Exports Grow 44% to USD 31.97 Billion in April–September FY 2026-27
subtitle:
Smartphone Exports Grow 35.8% to USD 18.17 Billion

Non-Smartphone Electronics Exports Rise 56.5% to USD 13.79 Billion in April–September FY 2026-27
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                17 NOV 2026 3:26PM by PIB Delhi
content:
India’s electronic goods exports registered strong growth of 44.0% during April–September FY 2026-27, increasing from USD 22.20 billion in the corresponding period of FY 2025-26 to USD 31.97 billion. While smartphones continued to account for the largest share of the electronics export basket, non-smartphone electronics recorded significantly faster growth, reflecting the broadening and diversification of India’s electronics exports across components, printed circuit boards, communication equipment, memory products and storage devices.
Exports of smartphones (HS 85171300) increased by 35.8%, from USD 13.38 billion in April–September FY 2025-26 to USD 18.17 billion during April–September FY 2026-27. Smartphones continued to be the largest component of India’s electronic goods exports. However, their share in total electronic goods exports moderated from 60.3% to 56.8%, amid faster growth in other electronics segments.
Non-smartphone electronics exports recorded a growth of 56.5%, increasing from USD 8.81 billion to USD 13.79 billion during the period. Consequently, the share of non-smartphone electronics in total electronic goods exports increased from 39.7% to 43.2%, indicating a broadening of India’s electronics export basket.
Exports of parts and accessories comprising mounted printed circuit boards (HS 84733030) increased from USD 63.3 million to USD 2.10 billion, registering growth of 3,219%. Singapore was the leading destination, with exports reaching USD 1.87 billion, followed by China at USD 111.5 million.
Exports of populated, loaded or stuffed printed circuit boards (HS 85177910) also registered significant growth of 304%, increasing from USD 213.7 million to USD 864.1 million. China was the leading destination at USD 789.2 million, while exports to Hong Kong increased from USD 5.9 million to USD 25.3 million.
Exports of network transmission and routing equipment (HS 85176290) nearly doubled, rising by 98% from USD 732.9 million to USD 1.45 billion. Hong Kong led the growth, with exports increasing from USD 264.7 million to USD 857.7 million. The United States and the Netherlands were also important destinations, with exports of USD 130.9 million and USD 124.4 million, respectively.
Exports of memory integrated circuits (HS 85423200) recorded growth of 2,333%, increasing from USD 23.1 million to USD 562.4 million. Malaysia emerged as the largest destination at USD 390.8 million, followed by Singapore at USD 102.4 million and Hong Kong at USD 25.2 million.
Similarly, exports of solid-state non-volatile storage devices (HS 85235100) increased by 1,680%, from USD 14.6 million to USD 260.5 million. China was the leading destination at USD 108.6 million, followed by Singapore at USD 76.8 million, Hong Kong at USD 22.3 million and the United States at USD 20.7 million.
The growth in India’s electronics exports reflects an increasingly diversified export basket, with non-smartphone electronics registering faster growth and gaining a larger share in overall exports. While smartphones continued to remain the largest component, with exports reaching USD 18.17 billion, the non-smartphone segment recorded stronger growth, increasing its contribution to total electronic goods exports.
The expansion across printed circuit boards, communication equipment, memory integrated circuits and solid-state storage devices, along with rising exports to markets such as Singapore, China, Hong Kong and Malaysia, underscores the growing contribution of these segments to India’s electronics export growth.

title: India and Egypt reaffirm commitment to strengthen bilateral trade, investment and industrial cooperation

content:
Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal concluded his official visit to the Arab Republic of Egypt from 15 to 16 November 2026. The visit marked his first bilateral visit to an African country. During the visit, the Minister held a series of high-level bilateral meetings, co-chaired the 7th Session of the India–Egypt Joint Trade Committee (JTC), participated in business engagements and interacted with representatives of the Indian and Egyptian business communities.
India and Egypt share longstanding relations rooted in historical, civilizational and people-to-people ties, which have evolved into a multifaceted partnership encompassing political, economic, security and cultural cooperation. Under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, India–Egypt relations have gained renewed momentum, culminating in the elevation of bilateral ties to a Strategic Partnership, with a shared commitment to enhanced cooperation in political, security, energy and economic fields.
The visit included the 7th Session of the India–Egypt JTC, the 6th India–Egypt Joint Business Council (JBC) Meeting and Business Forum, and the India–Egypt Startups Forum. During the visit, Shri Piyush Goyal called on Prime Minister of the Arab Republic of Egypt Dr. Mostafa Madbouly, held bilateral meetings with Egyptian Ministers and met leading business representatives in Egypt.
The visit provided renewed momentum to the longstanding India–Egypt economic partnership, with both sides reaffirming their commitment to expanding bilateral trade, promoting investments, strengthening industrial cooperation and enhancing business-to-business linkages. Both sides agreed to constitute a Working Group to discuss the modalities and framework for the Terms of Reference for entering into a mutually beneficial PTA/FTA or CEPA, after evaluating the gains for both sides, covering trade in goods, services and investment.
The 7th Session of the India–Egypt Joint Trade Committee was co-chaired by Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal and Minister of Investment and Foreign Trade of Egypt Dr. Mohamed Farid Saleh on 15 November 2026. The JTC was elevated to the Ministerial level, reflecting the growing importance of economic and commercial engagement between the two countries.
Both sides reviewed developments in bilateral trade and agreed to work towards achieving a target of USD 12 billion in bilateral trade. They emphasised the importance of diversifying the trade basket, promoting higher value-added exports, strengthening market access and addressing trade-related challenges.
Bilateral merchandise trade during April–September 2026 stood at USD 5.04 billion, registering growth of 64 per cent over the corresponding period of the previous year. India's exports to Egypt during FY 2025–26 stood at USD 3.87 billion, while imports from Egypt amounted to USD 2.60 billion (Source: DGCIS).
The discussions covered a broad range of areas, including agricultural and veterinary cooperation, pharmaceuticals and healthcare, engineering goods, chemicals and petrochemicals, fertilisers, textiles, MSMEs, customs, services, renewable energy, green hydrogen, food security, transport and logistics. Both sides underscored the importance of regular exchanges of business delegations, buyer missions, trade exhibitions and business-matching activities.
The two sides discussed concerns relating to GOEIC registration of Indian ceramic tile companies, outstanding commercial payments, trade remedies and participation of Indian companies in Egyptian public procurement tenders. The discussions also covered cooperation in standardisation and conformity assessment, agricultural market access, veterinary services and accreditation of Indian products.
Both sides reviewed investment opportunities in Egypt, particularly in the Suez Canal Economic Zone (SCZONE). Approximately 70 Indian companies are operating in Egypt, with investments of around USD 5 billion. The Egyptian side welcomed greater Indian participation in investment opportunities in sectors such as automotive and auto components, pharmaceuticals, chemicals, textiles, food processing, engineering, renewable energy and logistics.
The two sides also agreed to encourage industrial partnerships and joint ventures in renewable energy, green hydrogen, pharmaceuticals, fertilisers, textiles, automotive components and digital transformation. In the areas of digital technology and fintech, both sides acknowledged the potential of linking India's UPI with Egypt's Instapay, the positive role of trade in local currencies in enhancing exports, and leveraging India's Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI) to accelerate Egypt's digital transformation.
The Agreed Minutes of the 7th India–Egypt Joint Trade Committee were signed by both Ministers. The next meeting of the JTC will be held in New Delhi in 2028, or earlier, on a mutually convenient date.
On the first day of the visit, Shri Piyush Goyal participated in the 6th India–Egypt Joint Business Council meeting and the India–Egypt Business Forum alongside Minister of Investment and Foreign Trade of Egypt Dr. Mohamed Farid Saleh. The Joint Business Council meeting brought together over 250 members of the Indian and Egyptian business communities and provided an opportunity to identify new avenues for trade, investment and industrial collaboration.
Discussions covered chemicals and petrochemicals, pharmaceuticals and healthcare, food processing and agri-business, renewable energy and green hydrogen, infrastructure, ports and logistics, IT and digital technologies, textiles and automotive sectors. The India–Egypt Business Forum facilitated discussions on sectoral opportunities, investment prospects and business partnerships. The engagements underscored the importance of greater private-sector participation in translating the potential of bilateral economic relations into tangible business outcomes.
On 16 November 2026, Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal participated in the India–Egypt Startups Forum alongside Minister of Planning and Economic Development of Egypt Dr. Ahmed Rostom. The Forum brought together startups, incubators, accelerators, venture investors and representatives of relevant government agencies from both countries.
The Forum provided a platform for nearly 50 Indian and Egyptian startups to present their respective innovation ecosystems, exchange experiences and explore collaboration across identified sectors. As part of the Forum, Shri Piyush Goyal held a Startups' Roundtable, during which he interacted with Indian and Egyptian startups along with Minister of Planning and Economic Development of Egypt Dr. Ahmed Rostom. Indian founders presented their offerings for the Egyptian market and outlined the support they were seeking, including distribution partners, pilot projects, certification and local manufacturing. They also interacted with their Egyptian counterparts in related sectors.
During the visit, Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal called on Prime Minister of the Arab Republic of Egypt Dr. Mostafa Madbouly. He also held bilateral meetings with Minister of Investment and Foreign Trade of Egypt Dr. Mohamed Farid Saleh; Minister of Industry of Egypt Eng. Khaled Hashem; Minister of Foreign Affairs, International Cooperation and Egyptian Expatriates of Egypt Dr. Badr Abdelatty; Minister of Planning and Economic Development of Egypt Dr. Ahmed Rostom; and Minister of Transport of Egypt Lt. Gen. Eng. Kamel Wazir.
The discussions focused on strengthening bilateral trade and investment relations, promoting industrial cooperation, facilitating business engagements and exploring new opportunities in sectors of mutual interest, including port modernisation, shipbuilding, greenfield and brownfield airport development, and the construction of affordable, high-quality metro rail systems.
The Minister also interacted with Egyptian business leaders and CEOs of select Egyptian companies to explore opportunities for investment, partnerships and expansion of business operations between the two countries.
As part of the visit, the accompanying Indian business delegation interacted with representatives of the African Export-Import Bank (Afreximbank). The discussions covered the Bank's initiatives and potential areas of engagement, including project preparation, project finance, advisory and capital markets, export development, industrial parks and the Africa Trade Gateway. The interaction provided an opportunity to explore avenues for facilitating Indian business engagement in African markets and identifying potential areas of cooperation with the Bank.
Shri Piyush Goyal also interacted with members of the Egyptian Junior Businessmen Association (EJBA), comprising second- and third-generation entrepreneurs from leading Egyptian family businesses, along with Indian companies operating in Egypt and the accompanying Indian business delegation. The interaction focused on strengthening entrepreneurial linkages, promoting partnerships and exploring new opportunities for bilateral business cooperation.
During the visit, the Minister interacted with members of the Indian community and the Indian business community in Egypt at an event organised by the Indian Community Association in Egypt on 14 November 2026. He acknowledged the contribution of the Indian community in strengthening people-to-people and business ties between the two countries.
