title: Over 12,000 Devotees Pay Homage to the Sacred Relics of Shakyamuni Buddha at Golden Pagoda, Namsai, in the First Two Days
subtitle:
Cumulative Footfall at the Sacred Relics Exposition in Arunachal Pradesh Exceeds 78,000

Public Darshan to Continue from 6:00 AM to 4:00 PM until 20 November 2026

District Administration Announces Region-wise Schedule to Facilitate Public Darshan
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                17 NOV 2026 8:16AM by PIB Delhi
content:
The exposition of the Sacred Relics of Shakyamuni Buddha at the Golden Pagoda (Kongmu Kham), Namsai, Arunachal Pradesh, has received an overwhelming response from devotees. More than 12,000 devotees visited the exposition during its first two days, on 14 and 15 November 2026. They offered prayers, paid homage to the Sacred Relics and sought the blessings of Lord Buddha.
With more than 31,000 devotees visiting the exposition at Tawang and over 35,000 at Bomdila, the cumulative footfall across the three venues has exceeded 78,000 by the end of 15 November 2026.
Devotees from different parts of Namsai district and neighbouring regions have been gathering at the Golden Pagoda since the commencement of the exposition. Long queues of devotees reflect their deep faith and reverence for the Sacred Relics. The large turnout also reflects the enduring influence of Buddhist teachings and traditions in the region.
The exposition at Namsai marks the third and final phase of the Sacred Relics Exposition in Arunachal Pradesh, being held from 31 October to 21 November 2026.
The exposition commenced at the historic Gaden Namgyal Lhatse (Tawang Monastery) on 31 October 2026. Union Minister of Culture and Tourism Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat and Chief Minister of Arunachal Pradesh Shri Pema Khandu attended the inaugural ceremony. Venerable Buddhist monks and other distinguished guests were also present.
Following the conclusion of the exposition at Tawang on 7 November, the Sacred Relics were taken to Thubchog Gatsel Ling (TGL) Monastery, also known as Lower Gompa, in Bomdila. The six-day exposition at Bomdila was held from 8 to 13 November 2026.
The Sacred Relics arrived at Namsai on 14 November 2026. They were ceremonially received and enshrined at the Golden Pagoda. The Governor of Arunachal Pradesh, Lt Gen Kaiwalya Trivikram Parnaik (Retd.), inaugurated the exposition in the presence of Deputy Chief Minister Shri Chowna Mein and Shri Raghav Prasad Bhatnagar, Director General, International Buddhist Confederation (IBC). State Ministers, public representatives, Buddhist monks and other dignitaries attended the ceremony.
The exposition across Tawang, Bomdila and Namsai has brought the Sacred Relics closer to devotees from different parts of Arunachal Pradesh. It has also brought together people from different Buddhist traditions in a spirit of shared faith and devotion.
The Golden Pagoda, also known as Kongmu Kham, is an important centre of Theravada Buddhist faith and heritage in eastern Arunachal Pradesh. The Tai Khamti, Singpho and other communities of the region have preserved their rich Buddhist traditions over generations. Their monasteries, festivals, art and religious practices form an important part of India's Buddhist heritage.
Tawang and Bomdila are known for their Mahayana and Vajrayana Buddhist traditions. Namsai is known for its Theravada Buddhist heritage. The exposition at these three locations reflects the rich diversity of Buddhist traditions in Arunachal Pradesh.
The exposition at Namsai offers a special opportunity to devotees from eastern Arunachal Pradesh, Assam and other northeastern States to pay homage to the Sacred Relics. It also enables them to connect more closely with the life and teachings of Lord Buddha.
The district administration has made arrangements to facilitate the orderly participation of devotees. A region-wise schedule has been drawn up to ensure convenient access to the Sacred Relics.
The schedule for public darshan is as follows:
Date
Devotees from designated areas
16 November 2026
Lathao Circle and Namsai Circle
17 November 2026
Piyong Circle and Lekang Circle
18 November 2026
Changlang, Jairampur, Bordumsa, Miao, Diyun, Tirap and Longding
19 November 2026
Mechuka, Tuting, Gelling, Tezu, Anjaw (Meyor), Lower Dibang Valley and Defence Personnel
20 November 2026
Assam and all other northeastern States, along with devotees who could not visit on the preceding days
Devotees are encouraged to follow the designated schedule and cooperate with the district administration. These arrangements will help ensure smooth movement and convenient public darshan.
The Sacred Relics being exhibited in Arunachal Pradesh are preserved at the National Museum, New Delhi. They originate from Piprahwa in Siddharthnagar district of Uttar Pradesh. The site is associated with ancient Kapilavastu and the Shakya tradition of Lord Buddha.These relics are of exceptional historical, archaeological and spiritual significance. They are among the most precious objects of India's Buddhist heritage.
The tradition of venerating Sacred Relics began after the Mahaparinirvana of Lord Buddha. His Sacred Relics were enshrined in stupas, which became important centres of Buddhist pilgrimage and devotion.
The Sacred Relics have returned to Arunachal Pradesh after a gap of 13 years. Their exposition has provided devotees across the State with a cherished opportunity to pay homage to Lord Buddha and reconnect with their spiritual heritage.
Two special exhibitions are being held at the Meditation Centre of the Golden Pagoda. They have been organised by the National Museum, New Delhi, and the International Buddhist Confederation. The exhibition titled “Unearthing the Sacred Piprahwa: The Story of the Holy Buddha Relics and Their Discovery”, organised by the International Buddhist Confederation, presents the history and significance of the Piprahwa Relics.It traces their discovery at Piprahwa in Uttar Pradesh and the subsequent archaeological excavations. It also highlights the tradition of Buddhist relic veneration and the spiritual significance of the Sacred Relics.
The exhibition further presents the remarkable journey of the Piprahwa jewel collection. These precious objects returned to India in 2025 after more than a century. Their return marks an important achievement in the preservation and recovery of India's cultural heritage.
The second exhibition, titled “Crossroads of Dhamma: Classical Legacies, Living Art, and Anthropological Perspectives”, has been curated by the National Museum, New Delhi. It highlights the rich artistic and cultural heritage of Buddhism. It also presents the influence of Buddhist teachings on art, culture and living traditions.
Both exhibitions provide visitors with an opportunity to learn more about the life and teachings of Lord Buddha. They also help create awareness about the importance of protecting and preserving India's Buddhist heritage for future generations.
Under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, the Government of India has undertaken several initiatives to protect, preserve and promote India's Buddhist heritage.
Efforts are being made to improve infrastructure, connectivity and facilities at important Buddhist pilgrimage destinations. The Government has also promoted Buddhist scholarship, international conferences and cultural exchanges.
The recognition of Pali as a classical language in 2024 is an important step towards preserving Buddhist knowledge and literary traditions. The return of the Piprahwa jewel collection to India in 2025 is another significant achievement in safeguarding the country's Buddhist heritage.
In recent years, India has organised and supported expositions of Sacred Buddhist Relics in Mongolia, Thailand, Vietnam, Russia, Bhutan and Sri Lanka. These expositions have provided millions of devotees with opportunities to pay homage to the Sacred Relics. They have also strengthened India's cultural and spiritual ties with Buddhist communities across the world.
Earlier this year, the exposition of the Sacred Relics of Lord Buddha in Ladakh provided devotees in the Himalayan region with a special opportunity for public veneration.
The ongoing exposition in Arunachal Pradesh carries forward these efforts. It highlights the rich Buddhist heritage of the northeastern Himalayan region and the important role of its communities in preserving Buddhist traditions.
The exposition of the Sacred Relics of Shakyamuni Buddha is an occasion of immense spiritual and cultural significance. The participation of thousands of devotees reflects the enduring faith in Lord Buddha and His teachings.
For more than two millennia, the teachings of Lord Buddha have guided humanity towards peace, compassion, wisdom and non-violence. These values continue to hold great relevance in the contemporary world.
The exposition is being organised by the Ministry of Culture, Government of India, in collaboration with the Government of Arunachal Pradesh, the National Museum, New Delhi, and the International Buddhist Confederation (IBC), New Delhi.
Public darshan of the Sacred Relics will continue at the Golden Pagoda, Namsai, until 20 November 2026. Following the conclusion of the exposition, the Sacred Relics are scheduled to return to the National Museum, New Delhi, on 21 November 2026.

title: India to leverage Joint Crediting Mechanism with Japan to accelerate Low-carbon Transition, attract Investment and Strengthen Domestic Capabilities: Shri Bhupender Yadav at COP31 in Antalya (Türkiye)
ministry: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                17 NOV 2026 7:37PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Antalya (Türkiye), 17th November, 2026
Union Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Shri Bhupender Yadav, today highlighted the progress in operationalising the India-Japan Joint Crediting Mechanism (JCM), emphasising its potential to mobilise finance, facilitate technology transfer and advance low-carbon development. Addressing the 12th JCM Partner Countries' Meeting at the Japan Pavilion during UNFCCC COP31 in Antalya, Türkiye, the Minister said that mechanisms such as JCM can promote equitable and scalable climate cooperation while supporting the national priorities of developing countries.
Addressing the event, the Minister of Environment (Japan), H.E. Mr. Sasakawa Hiroyoshi highlighted that JCM holds tremendous potential to foster global partnerships in mobilising finance and leveraging technology to advance decarbonisation. It is a practical model to accelerate decarbonisation projects across the globe. Japan would extend all support and knowledge to its partners to achieve this goal, he stated. Ministers from other JCM partner countries including Oman, Mongolia, Palau, Papua New Guinea, Tunisia and Ukraine also presented their views during the event.
Highlighting the longstanding India-Japan partnership, Shri Yadav noted that the two countries signed a Memorandum of Cooperation on August 7, 2025, establishing the JCM under Article 6.2 of the Paris Agreement. The mechanism is expected to support India's Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC) and Long-Term Low Emission Development Strategy (LT-LEDS), with projects aligned with Government-approved activities and applicable JCM requirements. Beyond emission reductions, it is expected to strengthen domestic capabilities, skills and local value chains while generating wider sustainable development benefits.
The Minister highlighted significant progress in implementation, including the adoption of the Rules of Implementation by the Joint Committee on June 8, 2026, and the launch of the Operational Manual on September 30, 2026. The Manual establishes procedures for project submissions, methodology development, project design, sustainable development assessment, independent validation and verification, project registration, credit issuance and authorisation of mitigation outcomes.
Shri Yadav said India and Japan are working towards digitalising the JCM project cycle to streamline submissions, facilitate processing and enhance transparency. Immediate priorities include inviting applications for Third-Party Entities, receiving proposed methodologies and facilitating Project Idea Note submissions. He also underscored the importance of strengthening domestic validation and verification capacities to ensure robust monitoring, reporting and verification.
Reaffirming India's commitment to working closely with Japan, the Minister emphasised that the success of JCM should be measured not only by emission reductions but also by the finance mobilised, technologies transferred, domestic capacities strengthened and sustainable development benefits generated. He called for making the mechanism a model of transparent, equitable, environmentally robust and development-oriented climate cooperation.

title: India looks forward to Deepen Partnership with Small Island Developing States for Resilient Coasts and Oceans: Shri Bhupender Yadav at COP31 in Antalya (Türkiye)

ministry: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change

content:
Antalya (Türkiye), 17th November, 2026
Union Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Shri Bhupender Yadav, today called for strengthening India's partnership with Small Island Developing States (SIDS) to build resilient coasts and oceans through knowledge-sharing, technology partnerships and practical cooperation. Addressing the high-level ministerial event on
‘India–SIDS Partnership for Resilient Coasts and Oceans: Sharing Knowledge, Technology and Solutions’
during UNFCCC COP31 in Antalya, Türkiye, the Minister emphasised that healthy oceans and resilient coastlines are fundamental to economic security, ecological stability and people's well-being. The event was organised by The Energy and Resources Institute (TERI) and the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Government of India, in partnership with the International Solar Alliance (ISA). It saw participation at ministerial level from the island nations of Mauritius (H.E. Mr. Rajesh Anand Bhagwan), Kiribati (H.E Mr. Tokaibure Rabaua), Marshal Islands (H.E. Mr. Jess Gasper), besides senior officials from the Government of Fiji (Mr. Andrew K. Coriakula), TERI and ISA.
Highlighting the growing challenges of sea-level rise, coastal erosion, ocean warming, coral bleaching, stronger storms and marine pollution, Shri Yadav said these are immediate concerns for island nations, affecting homes, infrastructure, livelihoods and, in some cases, the long-term habitability of their territories. Guided by the vision of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi and the principle of
Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam
, India believes that environmental protection and development must advance together, with climate resilience centred on people, livelihoods and ecosystems, he stated. Sharing India's experience in coastal resilience, the Minister highlighted the country's approximately 11,099-kilometre coastline and its efforts in scientific assessment, ecosystem conservation, shoreline management and disaster preparedness. He cited the Mangrove Initiative for Shoreline Habitats and Tangible Incomes (MISHTI), which advances mangrove conservation and restoration while supporting coastal livelihoods.
The Minister further highlighted India's experience in scientific coastal assessments, ocean forecasting and early warning systems, particularly in the States of Odisha and Andhra Pradesh, as important areas for knowledge exchange with SIDS. Through the International Solar Alliance (ISA), Coalition for Disaster Resilient Infrastructure (CDRI), Infrastructure for Resilient Island States (IRIS) and Forum for India-Pacific Islands Cooperation (FIPIC), India is seeking to deepen cooperation in renewable energy, disaster preparedness, resilient infrastructure and locally appropriate climate adaptation solutions, he informed.
Identifying four priority areas for enhanced India–SIDS cooperation, Shri Yadav called for collaboration on coastal risk assessment, shoreline monitoring and early warning systems; Ecosystem-based approaches covering mangrove conservation, coral reef and seagrass protection, wetland restoration and sustainable management of coastal and marine resources; Technology partnerships for Island context, focused on solar-powered solutions, decentralised renewable energy, water security and climate-resilient infrastructure; and Institutional partnerships and capacity-building to support joint project preparation and country-led pilot initiatives.
The Minister emphasised that cooperation must be guided by the priorities and national circumstances of individual countries, with solutions adapted to their geography, ecosystems and institutional capacities. He also underlined the importance of mutual learning, noting that SIDS, as custodians of extraordinary marine biodiversity and traditional knowledge, have valuable experience in adapting to changing ocean conditions. Shri Yadav expressed confidence that the dialogue would help identify concrete opportunities for collaboration and build partnerships extending beyond the meeting. Reaffirming India's readiness to share its experience and technical capabilities while learning from the priorities and knowledge of SIDS, he called for moving from shared challenges to shared solutions and from dialogue to action to protect oceans, strengthen coastal communities and secure a resilient future for generations to come.

title: India and Sweden launch LeadIT 3.0 at COP31 to accelerate Low-carbon Industrial Transition; Brazil joins LeadIT as its newest Country Member
subtitle: LeadIT 3.0 to focus on Scaling Industrial Projects, Mobilising Capital and Delivering Tangible Outcomes from 2027 to 2030
ministry: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                17 NOV 2026 12:59PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Shri Bhupender Yadav, today announced the launch of the third phase of the Leadership Group for Industry Transition (LeadIT 3.0) at the Industry Leaders’ Roundtable during the United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31) in Antalya, Türkiye. The roundtable was co-chaired by Shri Yadav and H.E. Helena Dyrssen, State Secretary, Ministry of Climate and Enterprise, Sweden. Also present on the occasion was Mr. Selwin Hart, Special Advisor and Assistant Secretary-General, UN Climate Action.
Addressing the gathering, Shri Yadav highlighted that geopolitical conflicts, volatile energy markets and competing development priorities make international cooperation even more important, particularly in hard-to-abate industrial sectors. He emphasised that India’s priorities of poverty alleviation, energy access, job creation and infrastructure development must advance alongside its pursuit of a sustainable, low-carbon future.
Highlighting India's climate achievements, the Minister noted that the country has achieved a 37.38% reduction in emissions intensity between 2005 and 2022 and reached 50% non-fossil fuel-based installed electricity capacity, five years ahead of its target. India's additional forest carbon sink has also reached approximately 2.44 billion tonnes of CO₂ equivalent. India's achievements under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi were given a round of applause and the country's commitment was termed as a guiding light for other Nations in the fight against climate change. India's efforts in decarbonising hard to abate sectors was appreciated by Mr. Hart and the European Union.
Recalling LeadIT's progress since its launch by India and Sweden in 2019, Shri Yadav highlighted that its second phase facilitated eleven pre-pilot projects in steel and cement under the India-Sweden Industry Transition Partnership, besides expanding cooperation into low-carbon heavy-duty transport. The projects cover hydrogen-based ironmaking, electrification of industrial heat, carbon capture and utilisation, clinker substitution, industrial circularity and artificial intelligence to reduce cement demand. LeadIT has also supported South Africa's investment plan under the Climate Investment Funds and Ethiopia's engagement on low-carbon cement, he informed.
The Minister highlighted that LeadIT's membership has grown to 20 countries and 33 companies, and welcomed Brazil as its newest country member, strengthening the Global South's voice and opportunities for South-South cooperation. LeadIT 3.0, covering 2027–2030, would shift the focus from establishing partnerships to scaling industrial projects, mobilising capital and delivering tangible results. Its three priorities will be technology development and diffusion through industrial projects; capital mobilisation and de-risking to connect projects with finance; and capacity building and policy support, including carbon markets and workforce transition. Steel, cement and transport will remain core sectors, while the platform will remain open to new sectors and technologies.
Emphasising the need to move from feasibility studies to pilots, demonstration and replication, Shri Yadav called upon countries and companies to join the initiative and translate industrial transition commitments into action, highlighting that LeadIT 3.0 is being launched at COP31, which the Presidency has called the ‘COP of Implementation’. He stated that the transition must also create opportunities for workers, communities and developing economies. Concluding his remarks, the Minister underscored the importance of collective action in advancing the global industrial transition.

title: Big Cat Conservation can be a Powerful Pathway for Climate Change Mitigation: Union Environment Minister at UNFCCC COP31, at Antalya (Türkiye)
subtitle: India’s Tiger Conservation Model demonstrates how Wildlife Protection can strengthen Carbon Sinks, Climate Resilience and Community Livelihoods: Shri Bhupender Yadav
ministry: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                17 NOV 2026 1:04AM by PIB Delhi
content:
Antalya (Türkiye), 16th November, 2026
Union Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Shri Bhupender Yadav, today highlighted the critical role of big cat conservation in advancing climate change mitigation and strengthening ecosystem resilience at the High-Level Ministerial Side Event titled ‘BIG CATS: Drivers of Climate Change Mitigation’. The event was jointly organised by the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC), Government of India, and the International Big Cat Alliance (IBCA), at the United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31) in Antalya, Türkiye. The event brought together Ministers and country representatives from big cat range countries of Nepal, Venezuela, Cambodia, Sri Lanka, besides representatives of international conventions and organisations like the Ramsar Convention and UNCCD.
The gathering saw the dignitaries and conservation experts deliberate on the contribution of big cat conservation and their habitats towards climate change mitigation, ecosystem resilience and sustainable development. The discussions highlighted how conserving the world's seven major big cat species and their habitats can contribute to safeguarding carbon-rich ecosystems, strengthening ecosystem services, enhancing climate resilience and advancing global climate objectives. A presentation was also shown by DG (IBCA), Shri S.P. Yadav on the IBCA and status of big cats in the range countries. The participants appreciated India’s efforts made under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi in big cat conservation, especially Cheetah reintroduction.

The event brought together Ministers and country representatives from big cat range countries of Nepal, Venezuela, Cambodia, Sri Lanka, besides representatives of international conventions and organisations like the Ramsar Convention and UNCCD. 

The participants were appreciative of India’s efforts made under the leadership of PM Shri @narendramodi ji in big cat conservation, especially cheetah reintroduction.
— Bhupender Yadav (@byadavbjp)
November 16, 2026
Addressing the event, Shri Yadav highlighted the role of the International Big Cat Alliance (IBCA), envisioned by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, in advancing global big cat conservation. Recognising the challenges facing wildlife recovery globally, he said that IBCA provides a platform for sharing India's successful conservation models, facilitating knowledge exchange, strengthening international cooperation and building capacities for the recovery of all seven big cat species across the world. India's tiger conservation journey demonstrates how political commitment, strong institutions, sustained investment and community participation can transform wildlife conservation into an instrument of ecological security, climate resilience and sustainable development, he informed.
The Minister emphasized that big cat conservation provides a powerful pathway for protecting carbon-rich landscapes. The Minister stated that while big cats may not directly sequester carbon, their conservation helps protect forests, grasslands, wetlands and mountain ecosystems that store carbon, prevent emissions from habitat degradation and strengthen climate resilience. As umbrella species, big cats help mobilise the protection of entire ecosystems, benefiting thousands of other species and communities dependent on these landscapes. He stressed that wildlife conservation must be an integral component of nature-based climate action, complementing emission reduction efforts while delivering biodiversity, ecosystem and livelihood benefits.
Highlighting India's tiger conservation initiatives as an example of nature-based solutions, Shri Yadav stated that the country's 58 Tiger Reserves, spanning approximately 85,000 sq. km, protect extensive forest ecosystems and their carbon stocks. These landscapes provide vital ecosystem services, including carbon sequestration, water purification, soil conservation and groundwater recharge. Over 600 rivers originate or flow through these landscapes, underscoring the importance of tiger habitats as critical watersheds. The Minister also emphasised that community participation, eco-development and sustainable livelihood initiatives have made tiger conservation inclusive and sustainable.
Underscoring India's success in tiger conservation, Shri Yadav attributed it to sustained political commitment, strong legislation and robust institutional mechanisms. Project Tiger, supported by the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972 and the statutory body National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA), has provided a strong governance framework. India's tiger population increased to 3,682 in 2022, accounting for more than 70% of the world's wild tigers. This achievement has been supported by sustained Central and State budgetary allocations, dedicated frontline forest personnel, technology-enabled monitoring, scientific management and community stewardship. He further highlighted that Project Tiger generates livelihood opportunities of approximately 6 million man-days annually, making tiger conservation an important driver of green employment and community livelihood security.

title: President of India inaugurates Golden Jubilee celebrations of ICMR–National Institute of Malaria Research
subtitle:
India records nearly 80 per cent decline in malaria cases and deaths between 2015 and 2025: President

President calls for sustained vigilance, effective surveillance and community participation to achieve malaria elimination

Scientific research must reach every village and every community where it is needed: President Murmu

President highlights ICMR’s contribution to malaria research and indigenous vaccine development

Union Health Minister Shri J.P. Nadda calls for intensified efforts to achieve malaria elimination by 2030

Number of malaria high-burden districts falls from 155 to 33: Union Health Minister Shri Nadda

Union Health Minister underscores the role of research and innovation in making healthcare affordable and accessible

Secretary DHR and DG ICMR calls for strengthening research to address emerging challenges in malaria control

ICMR–NIMR marks five decades of scientific research and contribution to malaria control
ministry: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                17 NOV 2026 6:55PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The President of India, Smt. Droupadi Murmu, today inaugurated the Golden Jubilee celebrations of the Indian Council of Medical Research–National Institute of Malaria Research (ICMR–NIMR). Congratulating the past and present scientists, researchers and healthcare workers associated with the institute, the President recalled that malaria had historically been one of India's most serious public health challenges, particularly affecting rural and tribal communities. Sharing her personal experiences of witnessing the impact of malaria in villages, she highlighted how the disease affected people's livelihoods, education and future. She emphasised the importance of public awareness about completing the prescribed course of medication to ensure effective treatment and prevent recurrence.
The President highlighted India's progress in malaria control, noting that malaria cases and deaths had declined by nearly 80 per cent between 2015 and 2025, while the number of high-burden districts had reduced from 155 to 33. She also noted that 160 districts reported zero indigenous malaria cases during 2022–2025. Appreciating India's exit from the World Health Organization's (WHO) High Burden to High Impact (HBHI) group in 2024, she acknowledged the collective efforts of scientists, healthcare workers and citizens. She recognised ICMR–NIMR's contribution over five decades to research on malaria parasites, mosquito vectors, vector control, insecticide resistance and community surveillance.
Emphasising the need for continued vigilance and effective interventions, the President called for strengthened malaria diagnosis, treatment and surveillance, mosquito control, development of new medicines and vaccines, and greater public awareness and community participation. She stressed that scientific research and its outcomes should reach villages and communities where they are most needed. Drawing attention to emerging challenges such as climate change, unplanned urbanisation and increasing insecticide resistance among mosquitoes, she highlighted the importance of preventing waterlogging, eliminating mosquito breeding sources and strengthening environmental management. She also expressed satisfaction over ICMR–NIMR's contribution to the indigenous malaria vaccine being developed in Bhubaneswar and expressed confidence that it would support India's malaria elimination efforts.
The President also highlighted ICMR's contributions to research against tuberculosis, leprosy, kala-azar and COVID-19, including the establishment of a nationwide testing network and its partnership in the development of India's first indigenous COVID-19 vaccine. Referring to dengue as an emerging public health challenge, she called for effective research and diagnostic interventions. She also appreciated the role of the National One Health Mission in strengthening India's capacity to identify and address health risks emerging at the human-animal-environment interface. Emphasising the importance of indigenous medical technologies and affordable, quality healthcare, she called for stronger collaboration among research institutions, technical and higher education institutions and industry to realise the vision of Viksit Bharat by 2047.
Addressing the gathering, Union Minister of Health and Family Welfare Shri Jagat Prakash Nadda congratulated ICMR–NIMR on completing 50 years of dedicated scientific service. Describing the institute's contribution as a significant service to humanity, he appreciated its commitment to research and malaria prevention. He said that India's progress in malaria control over the past decade was the result of a comprehensive approach involving research on mosquito behaviour and malaria parasites, community participation, effective prevention, early diagnosis and appropriate treatment. Highlighting the decline of nearly 80 per cent in malaria cases between 2015 and 2025–26 and the reduction in high-burden districts from 155 to 33, he noted that India, which accounts for approximately 16 per cent of the global population, contributes around 0.7 per cent of global malaria cases and 0.6 per cent of malaria deaths. He appreciated India's exit from the WHO's High Burden to High Impact initiative and expressed confidence in achieving malaria elimination by 2030. “We will eliminate malaria by 2030 by bringing about the necessary changes in our strategies and policies,” he said, calling upon ICMR–NIMR to work with renewed commitment.
The Minister also appreciated ICMR's contributions to medical innovation, including MedTech Mitra, Patent Mitra and ELISA-based molecular diagnostics for dengue, chikungunya, Japanese encephalitis and other infectious diseases. Highlighting the Government's efforts to strengthen healthcare under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, he referred to the decline in out-of-pocket expenditure from 63 per cent to 42 per cent and the increase in government health expenditure from 6 per cent to 23 per cent. He called upon the scientific and healthcare community to intensify its efforts and contribute towards making India a leader in healthcare.
Secretary, Department of Health Research (DHR) and Director General, ICMR, Dr. Rajiv Bahl, highlighted ICMR–NIMR's 50-year journey since its establishment in 1977. He noted that the institute had evolved into one of India's premier institutions for malaria and vector-borne disease research, contributing to research on malaria vectors, parasite biology, insecticide resistance, treatment and diagnostics. He highlighted the Comprehensive Case Management Project in Odisha, undertaken in collaboration with the State Government, which demonstrated how universal access to testing, complete treatment and strengthened surveillance could substantially reduce malaria transmission, including in remote communities. He underlined the goals of zero indigenous malaria cases by 2027 and malaria elimination by 2030, and emphasised the need for stronger surveillance, interdisciplinary research and partnerships to address emerging challenges such as climate change, changing vectors and drug resistance. He reiterated ICMR's commitment to supporting research from basic scientific discovery and early-stage development to clinical evaluation of health technologies and interventions.
On this occasion, the President of India also released a commemorative postage stamp sheet marking the Golden Jubilee of ICMR–National Institute of Malaria Research, following its introduction by Ms. Mariamma Thomas, Member Postal Services Board.
The Union Minister of Health and Family Welfare released the ICMR–NIMR Coffee Table Book and the book
ICMR–NIMR Research Journey: Five Decades of Science, Service and Impact
. The first copies of the two books were presented to the President of India.
On the occasion, Director of ICMR-NIMR Dr Anup Anvikar highlighted the journey of NIMR in last 50 years through a video film depicting the Institute’s contribution in Malaria elimination efforts.
The Golden Jubilee celebrations mark five decades of ICMR–NIMR's contribution to malaria research and public health in India.

title: Himalayan Horizons Light Up IFFI 2026: Ladakhi and Kashmiri Stories Take Centre Stage
subtitle: From a young skater's dream on Ladakh's frozen ice to the children of Gulmarg and the last master woodcarvers of Srinagar, four films bring the spirit of the Himalayas to Goa
content:
Goa, 17 November 2026
The mountains, monasteries, snowbound villages and living crafts of the Himalayan region will find a vivid voice at the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) in Goa. Four films in Ladakhi and Kashmiri, including two feature films and two non-feature films, will bring the region’s landscapes, traditions and everyday human stories to festival audiences. Becoming, the Ladakhi short that serves as the Opening Film of the Indian Panorama Non-Feature section, sets the tone for the selection.
Ladakhi Films:
Becoming
, written and directed by Leena Yadav, is an 11-minute Ladakhi film that opens the Indian Panorama Non-Feature Films section. Set in Ladakh, it follows Rinchen, a young mother, and her son Agyal, who shows an unusual connection with nature from infancy. At the age of seven, Agyal experiences strange visions, feels drawn to the ancient Likir Monastery and recalls memories that seem to belong to another life. At the monastery, he identifies a box kept in a locked room, and the objects inside lead the monks to believe that he is the reincarnation of a respected Rimpoche. As Agyal begins his spiritual journey, the film explores rebirth, destiny and the links between past, present and future. The cast includes Rinchen Angmo and Tsering Wanggail. Leena Yadav is the award-winning writer, director and producer of Parched, Rajma Chawal and House of Secrets, as well as the Oscar-nominated Tell It Like a Woman.
Still from Becoming
Birds on Ice
, directed by Sahil Shah, is an 85-minute Ladakhi feature film selected for the Indian Panorama Feature Films section and the Best Debut Feature Film of a Director category. Tashi, a young girl from Ladakh, lives with her grandfather while waiting for her shepherd parents to return. When she gets a pair of borrowed ice-hockey skates, a new dream takes shape. As she faces the challenges of growing up in the harsh Himalayan winter, she discovers difficult truths about family, grief and survival. Determined not to give up, Tashi and her best friend find their own way to pursue her dream. The film stars Semzang Skitdon as Tashi, alongside N. Chopal, Kunga Choskyab, Padma Chorol and Sonam Stobgais. Written by Shaan Pasricha and produced by Cameo Films, it marks the feature debut of Sahil Shah, whose first film is shaped by the ice-hockey community.
Still from Birds on Ice
Kashmiri Films:
Sledge
, directed by Raja Shabir Mohammad Khan, is a 75-minute Kashmiri feature film that will have its Asia Premiere at IFFI 2026. It is featured in the Indian Panorama section and competes for Best Debut Director of an Indian Feature Film. In a snow-covered village near Gulmarg, Ali’s wooden sledge is his family’s only source of income. When he leaves home for a few days, his three children, Haziq, Eashel and Raima, are left with a freedom they don’t fully understand. In a moment of play, they accidentally break the sledge. Desperate to repair it before their father returns, the children venture into the tourist world of Gulmarg, trying to earn money while enduring rejection and quiet humiliations. When they find a lost bag filled with money and chocolates, the solution seems within reach, but the temptation to use it collides with the growing weight of their conscience. Raja Khan is a Satyajit Ray Film and Television Institute alumnus whose documentary Shepherds of Paradise won the National Award. The film is produced by Ryhana Productions and stars Haziq Mohammad Khan, Eashel Khan and Raima Khan.
Still from Sledge
Naqsh-e-Daur
, a 12-minute Kashmiri documentary in the Indian Panorama Non-Feature Films section, is directed by Baba Tassaduq Hussain, who also serves as cinematographer. In the old streets of Srinagar, Ghulam Nabi Dar continues the traditional Kashmiri craft of walnut woodcarving, a skill he has practised for over six decades. Honoured with the Padma Shri, he creates detailed designs that reflect the region’s history and culture. The film follows his life and work, showing his dedication to keeping the art alive in a changing world. As fewer people take up the craft, he remains committed to practising it and passing his knowledge on to the next generation, ensuring that Kashmir’s woodcarving tradition continues. The film is produced by BBP Studio Virtual Bharat Pvt Ltd, with the story by Bharatbala.

title: Stories Without Borders: Exploring Tamil and Telugu Cinema at IFFI 2026
content:
Goa, 17 November 2026
Tamil and Telugu cinema feature prominently at the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) 2026, presenting a diverse range of narratives exploring social issues, family relationships, human values, personal struggles and cultural traditions. The selection brings together stories from both languages across feature and non-feature categories, addressing themes ranging from technology and education to environmental conservation, family relationships, individual aspirations and political life.
Have a look at the Tamil Films
The Tamil selection includes stories set against both contemporary and traditional social settings.
Scroll
, directed by Kannan S, follows Aravind, a young man addicted to his smartphone, whose life takes a disturbing turn after he joins an app called Dopa Rush. The app challenges users to overcome smartphone addiction through a series of tasks and rewards. However, as the challenges become increasingly strange and disturbing, the game begins to control the participants' lives, transforming an attempt to break an addiction into a frightening experience.
Family relationships and unresolved conflicts form the central theme of
Thaai Kizhavi (God Mother)
, directed by Sivakumar Murugesan. The film tells the story of Pavunuthaayi, a strong-willed 70-year-old woman living with her daughter and grandson in a small village. Feared by some and respected by others, she has been separated from her three sons for many years. When she suddenly falls seriously ill, her sons return home, bringing back unresolved family conflicts and painful memories. As the past resurfaces, a long-hidden secret gradually comes to light, changing the family's understanding of their relationships.
Addressing the issue of access to education,
Arivu
, directed by Sathyashiva, is set in 1996 and follows Kathir, a young teacher posted to a remote tribal village in the Western Ghats. He discovers that girls are denied education because villagers believe it will anger the village deity. Determined to change this, he secretly teaches a group of girls aged 13–14 who have never attended school. As their examinations approach, Kathir helps them overcome their fears and social restrictions, enabling them to take their first steps towards education.
The Tamil selection also explores indigenous knowledge and traditional practices.
Attappadi
, directed by Vijeesh Mani, explores the traditional healing practices of indigenous communities in Kerala's Western Ghats. The film follows Sultan Ahmed Al Mehmoudi, who travels from Arabia to explore the medicinal knowledge and forest traditions preserved by the people of Attappadi. Guided by filmmaker Vijeesh Mani, he meets traditional healers and elders and learns about their relationship with the forest. What begins as a search for medicinal knowledge develops into a journey into the community's way of life and heritage.
Environmental conservation and community participation are central to
Koodu (Nest)
, directed by Joyal Vijay. Set in Vachathi, Tamil Nadu, a power cut leads to the discovery of a sparrow's nest with eggs inside a village transformer. Guided by village head Agathiyan, agriculture graduate Kathir and the villagers decide to remain without electricity for 35 days to protect the birds. Their decision faces strong opposition and attempts at sabotage by the local VAO and Lingam, driven by personal grudges. Despite these challenges, Kathir and the villagers make difficult sacrifices to keep the nest safe.
Check out the Telugu Films
The Telugu selection presents stories addressing environmental concerns, family relationships, love, personal aspirations, human values and politics.
Sing Geetham (Sing a Song)
, directed by Singeetham Srinivasa Rao, follows Pratap Mannem, who returns to the mining village of Kuberpuram to claim his share of the gold mines left by his father. He soon clashes with a former business partner whose expansion plans threaten to destroy the village's last tree. As greed and conflict spread, Pratap discovers the truth about his family's past and begins to change. The villagers eventually realise the importance of unity, sacrifice and protecting nature.
Family relationships, separation and reconciliation are explored in
Mana Shankara Vara Prasad Garu (Our Mr. Shankar Varaprasad)
, directed by Anil Ravipudi. The family drama centres on Shankar Vara Prasad, a dedicated national security officer, who puts his duty before his family, resulting in separation from his wife and children. Six years later, he attempts to rebuild their relationship by joining the school where his children study. When his family faces a serious threat, he is assigned to protect them. As he uncovers the danger, he must confront his past, save his loved ones and win back their trust.
Love and loss form the subject of
Chennai Love Story
, directed by Ravi Varma Namburi. The film follows Nivi, who is struggling to overcome the pain of a past relationship. She meets Steven, an orphan whose love and kindness gradually bring happiness back into her life. Despite their differences, they fall in love and decide to marry. However, Steven dies in an accident on their wedding day. Unable to accept his sudden loss, Nivi is overwhelmed by grief and anger, struggling to understand why he had to leave her despite his promise to stay by her forever.
The pursuit of personal aspirations is the focus of
Why, Vani?
, directed by Dhanush Dandu. The film tells the story of Vani, a young editor in Hyderabad who feels unfulfilled in her career. When she gets an opportunity to work on a documentary in Mumbai, she decides to pursue her dream of filmmaking. However, her decision creates challenges in her relationships with her boyfriend Arun and filmmaker Sahith, whose compromises on the project reflect their own fears. Struggling with family expectations and guilt, Vani eventually gains a renewed understanding of her choices and follows her dream.
Win
, directed by Praveen, explores the importance of perspective and self-discipline through the game of chess. The film centres on Napoleon, an 18-year-old who wants to win every chess game after years of strict training by his mother. Confident in his abilities, he enters a major chess tournament but loses to Gayatri, a calm ten-year-old girl. Unable to accept defeat, he challenges her again. Through their conversations, Gayatri helps him understand that playing well matters more than winning. She introduces him to the teachings of the Bhagavad Gita, encouraging him to perform his duty without becoming attached to the result. Napoleon gradually learns to control his ego and view chess differently.
Politics, ideology and the dynamics of friendship form the backdrop of
Mayasabha
, directed by Deva Katta. Set in Andhra Pradesh from the mid-1970s, the series follows two young men, Kakarla Krishnama Naidu (KKN), an idealistic student leader, and M.S. Rami Reddy (MSR), a young man from a powerful family. Despite their different backgrounds, they become friends and enter politics with hopes of bringing change. However, they soon encounter the realities of political life, including caste divisions, corruption, money and power struggles. As their influence grows, their ideals are tested and personal ambitions begin to affect their friendship. The series explores politics, ideology, power and whether two friends can remain united when competing for the same position.
Bhakta Kannappa
: A Golden Jubilee Celebration
The Telugu film selection also includes a special presentation in the Golden Jubilee section of IFFI 2026.
Bhakta Kannappa
, directed by Bapu, marks 50 years since its release on 26 May 1976. The restored print returns as part of the Festival's Golden Jubilee celebration.
The film retells the legend of Kannappa Nayanar, the legendary Shaiva devotee. Arjuna is reborn as Thinnadu, an atheist hunter raised by a tribal chief. He wins the hand of the chief's daughter, Neela, but his refusal to bow before the village deity forces him to leave his people. His life changes when he meets Lord Shiva and gradually learns the true depth of devotion. In the climax, he gives his own eyes to stop the Shiva Lingam from bleeding, an act that carries devotion beyond ritual and convention. Originally filmed in Kannada, the film won the National Film Award for Best Audiography and is remembered for its grandeur and outdoor scale.
Together, these stories reaffirm the spirit of this year's theme,
Stories Without Borders
. Told in Tamil and Telugu, they travel far beyond the linguistic and cultural worlds in which they are rooted. Whether exploring the struggles of a young teacher, the bonds of family, the pursuit of dreams, the protection of nature, the complexities of political life or the timeless power of devotion, these films speak to experiences and emotions that audiences everywhere can relate to. They remind us that while language may shape the way a story is told, it need not limit how it is understood or felt. Through these diverse cinematic voices, IFFI celebrates the power of cinema to transcend linguistic and cultural boundaries, bringing stories from different worlds closer to audiences everywhere.

title: IFFI 2026 Celebrates Kannada and Tulu Cinema
subtitle: Spotlights Girish Kasaravalli's 50-Year Cinematic Journey
content:
Goa, 17 November 2026
From the socially conscious parallel cinema of Girish Kasaravalli to contemporary family dramas, folklore-rooted epics and documentary storytelling, the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) is bringing the richness and diversity of Kannada and Tulu cinema into focus in Goa.
Kannada Films:
Kantara: A Legend
-
Chapter 1
, directed by and starring Rishab Shetty, is set during the Kadamba era. Berme, a young forest dweller, enters the neighbouring kingdom of Bangra and witnesses the harsh treatment of forest communities by its rulers. When Prince Kulashekara attacks the tribes and kills many of their people, Berme joins them in their fight for justice and dharma. The story brings together folklore, faith and a struggle to protect the forest communities. The film is featured in both Indian Panorama’s Mainstream Cinema section and the International Competition.
Ruby-Cube
, directed by P. Sheshadri, follows three generations of a family during a short holiday at a hill station. Rohini, a psychologist, reunites with her estranged husband Moorthy through their daughter Chitra, who is facing difficulties in her marriage. As the family spends time together, old tensions and unresolved emotions come to the surface. A Rubik’s Cube becomes a symbol of the complexities of relationships, showing how patience and understanding can help people find a way forward.
The Hug of Emptiness
, directed by Dr. Pradeep Kenchanuru (Dr. Pradeep Kumar Shetty K), tells the story of Chandrashekhar, whose property was taken over by the Sullia Cooperative Bank in 2003 after he failed to repay a loan. Believing the action to be unjust, he begins a legal battle that continues for more than two decades. Without a permanent home, he lives in his car while pursuing justice. The documentary portrays his long struggle, loneliness and determination in the face of an uncertain future.
Ulididdu Sampige Maatra (
Only the Flower Remained)
, directed by Abhishek, follows Manjanna, who lives alone with memories of a woman he loved and lost. When a photograph of her is damaged, he approaches an artist and asks him to recreate her portrait from memory. After receiving the painting, Manjanna meets a mysterious stranger. The unexpected encounter changes the way he looks at his past and leads him towards an ending he had not imagined. The short film explores loss, remembrance and emotional change.
Tulu Films:
Pili Channe
, directed by Anupama Sharadhi, follows a tribal woman who learns traditional herbal healing from her grandmother. Before her death, the grandmother gives her a sacred stone believed to carry the healing knowledge of the forest. Pili Channe uses her skills to help her community, earning their trust. When a greedy village doctor and the village chief try to take the stone for themselves, she refuses to give it up. The film explores traditional wisdom, courage and the protection of ancestral knowledge. It will have its World Premiere at IFFI 2026.
Special Session on Girish Kasaravalli:
IFFI 2026 will also host an in-conversation session titled
“The Moral Universe of Parallel Cinema: 50 Years of Girish Kasaravalli”
on 21 November. Moderated by Naman Ramachandran, the session will look back at five decades of filmmaking by the acclaimed Kannada director. From his debut film Ghatashraddha to works such as Tabarana Kathe, Thaayi Saheba and Dweepa, Kasaravalli’s films have explored social injustice, moral choices and the lives of marginalised people. The conversation will examine his approach to storytelling and the relationship between cinema and social conscience.

title: Northeast Cinema Finds its Spotlight at 57th IFFI with Four Indian Panorama Selections
subtitle:
Urum and Surjyamukhi set for World Premiere in the Feature Film section

Red Carpet and Chalo India With Eric Ji – Mizoram take the Northeast’s cultural stories to the Non-Feature Film canvas
content:
Goa, 17 November 2026
The diverse cultures, compelling stories and distinctive cinematic voices of Northeast India will find a prominent place at the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI), with four films from the region selected for the prestigious Indian Panorama section. Scheduled to be held in Goa from November 20 to 28, 2026, IFFI will showcase two feature films and two non-feature films from the Northeast, offering audiences a glimpse into the region’s indigenous heritage, social transformations and everyday lives.
Leading the feature film selection is
Urum (Spirit)
, which marks a historic milestone as the first Nyishi-language film to be selected for IFFI Indian Panorama. Directed by Duyu Tabyo, this psychological thriller from Arunachal Pradesh is also slated for its World Premiere at the festival. Set in a remote mountain village in Arunachal Pradesh, the film explores indigenous memory, trauma and concealed truths through the story of a father haunted by visions and guilt following the loss of his young daughter.
Joining
Urum
in the feature film lineup for its World Premiere is
Surjyamukhi (Sunflower)
, an Assamese drama directed by actor-director and theatre practitioner Antara G.G. Choudhury. Set against an urban backdrop, the film follows two young colleagues, Pushpal and Prarthana, whose initial rivalry gradually gives way to friendship and romance. However, the discovery of a lost bag of money sets off a series of unexpected moral dilemmas, testing their choices and relationships.
The Indian Panorama Non-Feature Film section brings two distinct stories from Assam and Mizoram.
Red Carpet
, a 30-minute Assamese documentary written and directed by award-winning filmmaker Aimee Baruah celebrates the enduring legacy of traditional handloom craftsmanship. Set in the Karbi Anglong hills of Assam, the film follows a Karbi weaver from the village of Donkamokam on an extraordinary journey to the red carpet at Cannes. Through her story, the documentary highlights the resilience of indigenous artisans, the richness of Karbi weaving traditions and the importance of preserving ancestral crafts.
The other non-feature selection,
Chalo India With Eric Ji - Mizoram
, is a 48-minute English documentary directed by Rajdeep Choudhury. The film follows former British Member of Parliament and history teacher Eric Ollerenshaw OBE as he explores the social and cultural landscape of Mizoram. It offers a window into the state's high literacy levels, civic discipline and vibrant football culture, while also highlighting the significant contributions of Mizo women in business, education and community leadership.

title: Tribal communities have been the guardians of biodiversity: Dr Jitendra Singh
subtitle:
Dr Jitendra Singh addresses ‘Janjatiya Gaurav Divas’ programme organised by Ministry of Science & Technology

Tribal knowledge and STEM training can shape India’s scientific progress: Dr Jitendra Singh

Affordable, locally suited technologies can strengthen tribal economies, says the Union Minister

Technology compendium and booklet on STI for Tribal Empowerment released
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                17 NOV 2026 4:52PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science and Technology and Earth Sciences, and Minister of State in the Prime Minister’s Office, the Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions, the Department of Atomic Energy and the Department of Space, Dr Jitendra Singh, today called for tribal communities to be partners and leaders in India’s scientific and innovation journey.
Dr Jitendra Singh was addressing a programme marking Janjatiya Gaurav Divas, commemorating the birth anniversary of Bhagwan Birsa Munda. The programme was organised by the Department of Science and Technology’s (DST) SEED Division and the North East Centre for Technology Application and Reach (NECTAR). A technology compendium and a booklet on science, technology and innovation for tribal empowerment were released on the occasion.
Dr Jitendra Singh said Bhagwan Birsa Munda remains one of the greatest icons of India’s freedom struggle and a symbol of courage, self-respect and the aspirations of tribal communities. His life and contribution, the Minister said, continue to inspire efforts towards social justice, equality and inclusive development.
The Minister described tribal communities as guardians of biodiversity, living in harmony with forests, rivers and mountains. Dr Jitendra Singh said tribal knowledge and practices continue to inspire modern science, while digital education and STEM training can help tribal youth lead India’s scientific journey. The Minister called for technology-based enterprises, supported by skills, mentoring, finance and market linkages, to create livelihoods and strengthen local economies, particularly in the North Eastern Region.
The Minister said that the empowerment of tribal communities, particularly those living in remote and geographically challenging regions, is essential to achieving the vision of Viksit Bharat @2047.
The Union Minister emphasised the need for affordable, accessible technologies suited to local conditions and easy to operate and maintain. Citing sickle cell anaemia, Dr. Singh referred to a multi-institutional CRISPR-Cas9 gene therapy effort involving CSIR-IGIB, AIIMS New Delhi, CSIR-IICT Hyderabad, NII Mumbai and other institutions.
Dr Jitendra Singh said that Prof.Umesh V. Waghmare and the Department of Science and Technology had accomplished considerable work over the past few years to support Scheduled Tribe communities. He cited 124 new projects that benefited more than 75,000 people, particularly members of Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups, and 25 dedicated Science, Technology and Innovation (STI) Hubs across the country. Eleven Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe cells have also been set up in different States. Natural resource management programmes have benefited over 20,000 members of Scheduled Tribe communities.
The Union Minister said DST had also invited proposals to establish NIDHI Technology Business Incubator (TBI) hubs to promote startups with at least one founder from a Scheduled Tribe community. Dr Singh said there was immense talent waiting to emerge from these communities, which were not seeking charity but their due share of opportunities. He cited the INSPIRE-MANAK programme, in which 21,087 students from Scheduled Tribe communities in Classes 6 to 12 participated, forming a large share of the overall awardees.
Prof.Umesh V. Waghmare, Secretary, DST, said Janjatiya Gaurav Divas was an occasion to remember other tribal leaders who contributed to India’s freedom struggle and national development, and to acknowledge the contributions of tribal communities. He said working with tribal communities and including all sections of society are essential for the sustainable growth of the nation.
Prof. Ajay Sood, Principal Scientific Adviser to the Government of India, highlighted India’s strong research ecosystem and the potential to bring its technologies to communities at scale. Citing RuTAG and Rural Smart Village Centers, he said tribal communities, women and local entrepreneurs can lead technology-based enterprises that strengthen livelihoods and local economies.
The exhibition organised alongside the programme showcased innovative technologies and interventions developed through projects supported by DST and NECTAR for the benefit of tribal communities.
Dr Jitendra Singh congratulated DST and all the institutions and stakeholders associated with the programme, and reaffirmed the need to ensure that the benefits of India’s scientific and technological progress reach every corner of the country and every section of society.

title: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment’s Pavilion at 45th IITF 2026
subtitle:
Records Cumulative Sales of ₹17.37 Lakh; Growing Consumer Response Strengthens Livelihood Opportunities for Traditional Artisans

Over 130 Artisans from 19 States Showcase India’s Rich Handicraft, Handloom and Indigenous Artistic Heritage
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                17 NOV 2026 7:39PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Reflecting growing consumer appreciation for indigenous craftsmanship and traditional handmade products, the pavilion of the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment at the ongoing 45th India International Trade Fair (IITF) 2026 at Bharat Mandapam, in the National Capital here, has recorded cumulative sales of ₹17.37 lakh as of November 16, 2026.
The cumulative sales have witnessed a more than threefold increase from approximately ₹5.50 lakh recorded up to November 15, 2026, highlighting the encouraging consumer response and expanding market opportunities for participating artisans and entrepreneurs.
The Ministry’s pavilion, located at Hall No. 5, Ground Floor, ITPO, continues to bring together traditional craftsmanship, cultural diversity and entrepreneurial talent from across the country, providing artisans with opportunities to connect directly with consumers, enhance product visibility and strengthen their economic prospects.
A Senior Official in the Ministry said more than 130 artisans from 19 States are showcasing their products at the ongoing Trade Fair through the Ministry’s three Apex Corporations, namely the National Scheduled Castes Finance and Development Corporation (NSFDC), National Backward Classes Finance and Development Corporation (NBCFDC) and National Safai Karamcharis Finance and Development Corporation (NSKFDC).
He said the pavilion showcases a diverse range of intricately crafted handicrafts, traditional handlooms, handcrafted jewellery, footwear, textiles, handmade articles and other indigenous products, reflecting the rich cultural heritage and artistic traditions of different regions of the country.
The Official said the significant increase in cumulative sales reflects growing consumer appreciation for traditional products and highlights the importance of national-level exhibitions in creating market-oriented livelihood opportunities for artisans and small entrepreneurs.
He said beyond facilitating the direct sale of products, the Trade Fair provides an opportunity for participating artisans to understand changing consumer preferences, explore emerging market trends, establish new business connections and identify opportunities for long-term entrepreneurial growth.
The Official said such platforms play an important role in bridging the gap between traditional producers and mainstream markets, enabling artisans to translate their skills, creativity and indigenous knowledge into sustainable income-generating opportunities.
He said guided by the vision of Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi and the principle of
‘Sabka Saath, Sabka Vikas’
, the Ministry continues to facilitate greater economic participation of artisans and entrepreneurs belonging to Scheduled Castes, Backward Classes, Safai Mitras and De-Notified, Nomadic and Semi-Nomadic Tribes (DNTs).
The Official said an important highlight of the Ministry’s participation at IITF 2026 is the promotion of the TULIP (Traditional Artisans’ Upliftment Livelihood Programme) brand, which aims to build a distinct market identity for artisan-made products and strengthen their recognition among domestic and international consumers.
The TULIP initiative was recently launched by Hon’ble Union Minister for Social Justice and Empowerment, Dr. Virendra Kumar, during the Shilp Samagam Mela at Dilli Haat in the National Capital, he said.
The Official said the initiative seeks to connect traditional craftsmanship with contemporary market requirements while encouraging innovation, entrepreneurship and economic self-reliance among artisans.
Through the promotion of TULIP and participation in prominent national-level exhibitions, the Ministry is working towards creating an enabling ecosystem wherein traditional artisans can expand their market presence, strengthen their entrepreneurial capabilities and access sustainable livelihood opportunities, he said.
The Official said the participation of the Ministry’s three Apex Corporations at IITF 2026 further highlights their significant role in facilitating market access, promoting entrepreneurship and strengthening the socio-economic standing of beneficiaries from disadvantaged and marginalised communities.
He said visitors to the Ministry’s pavilion have an opportunity to explore India’s diverse artistic heritage, interact directly with artisans and contribute to their economic empowerment by purchasing authentic, indigenous and handcrafted products.
The ongoing 45th India International Trade Fair 2026, inaugurated on November 13, 2026, provides a prominent platform for trade, commerce, entrepreneurship and cultural exchange, bringing together producers and consumers from diverse backgrounds.
With the encouraging sales performance and growing consumer engagement at IITF 2026, the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment continues to reinforce its commitment to preserving India’s cultural heritage, strengthening sustainable livelihoods, fostering economic self-reliance and advancing inclusive socio-economic development in line with the vision of
Viksit Bharat@2047
.

title: Stage Set for ‘Samaveshi Niti Sankalp’: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment Ready to Welcome Delegates from States, Union Territories for Two-Day Departmental Summit
subtitle:
Extensive Preparations Completed for November 18–19 Summit in National Capital

Focus on Strengthening Centre-State Partnership for Inclusive Socio Economic Development

Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi to Grace the Valedictory Session

More Than 13,500 Responses from Over 450 Districts to Shape Policy Deliberations and Strengthen Ground-Level Implementation
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                17 NOV 2026 6:06PM by PIB Delhi
content:
With preparations in place and the stage set for a significant national-level dialogue on social justice and inclusive development, the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment is all set to welcome delegates, senior officials and representatives from States and Union Territories for the two-day Departmental Summit titled
‘Samaveshi Niti Sankalp’
, scheduled to begin tomorrow, at Sushma Swaraj Bhawan, in the National Capital here.
The Ministry has completed the necessary preparations for the Summit, which will bring together representatives of the Union, State & UT Governments on a common platform to deliberate on key policy priorities, strengthen institutional coordination and work towards more effective implementation of welfare programmes.
The Summit will focus on advancing the vision of
Viksit Bharat@2047
through a stronger Centre-State Partnership and a shared commitment to inclusive development.
The Hon’ble Prime Minister, Shri Narendra Modi, is scheduled to grace the Valedictory Session of the Summit, where the key outcomes and time-bound action plans emerging from the deliberations will be presented.
Secretary, Ministry of Social Justice And Empowerment, Shri Sudhansh Pant said the Departmental Summit is the third in a series of such summits envisioned by the Hon’ble Prime Minister to encourage collective ownership of national priorities, facilitate exchange of experiences and accelerate development outcomes through coordinated efforts between the Centre and the States.
He said in the run-up to the Summit, the Ministry has undertaken extensive consultations with State and Union Territory administrations, field-level functionaries and other stakeholders to ensure that policy discussions are informed by practical experiences and implementation-related insights.
The Secretary said a series of video conferences were held with State and Union Territory officials, while feedback was sought on four identified thematic areas from stakeholders within and outside the Government.
The consultation exercise received an encouraging response, with more than 13,500 responses from over 450 districts across the country, Shri Pant said. These valuable inputs have been incorporated into the background notes prepared for the Summit to facilitate informed, focused and outcome-oriented deliberations, he said.
Shri Sudhansh Pant said the Departmental Summit provides an important institutional platform for the Centre and States to come together, share successful practices, identify implementation challenges and explore innovative approaches for strengthening the delivery of welfare initiatives.
He said that the objective is to translate discussions into actionable strategies, with clearly defined timelines and shared responsibilities, ensuring that the benefits of government programmes reach their intended beneficiaries effectively.
The two-day Summit will deliberate on four key thematic areas namely
‘Reimagining Prevention and Drug Demand Reduction Strategy for a Nasha Mukt Bharat’
;
‘One Nation, One Scholarship Portal – Accessible Scholarships’
;
‘Empowered Students, Early Intervention and Reduction of Disability Burden’
and ‘Sugamya Bharat for Viksit Bharat’, Shri Pant further said.
The Secretary said these themes reflect the Ministry's continued focus on strengthening social inclusion, expanding access to welfare initiatives, improving institutional mechanisms and promoting the empowerment of aspirational sections of society.
The Secretary said the deliberations will be organised through four breakout sessions and two full-house sessions, providing opportunities for comprehensive discussions on the identified themes. He said all States and Union Territories will have dedicated opportunities and slots to make presentations during the breakout sessions and share their perspectives and comments in the full-house discussions.
Two experts will also share insights on international best practices to enrich the deliberations and encourage innovative approaches to programme implementation, he said.
Shri Pant said an important highlight of the Summit will be a
Digital Exhibition
showcasing the Ministry's key initiatives, flagship programmes and technology-driven interventions.
He said the Delegates will have the opportunity to explore integrated digital platforms such as ‘Samavesh’ and ‘e-Anudan’, Mobile Applications developed for field-level operations, and success stories demonstrating the impact of various schemes and programmes.
The exhibition will highlight how digital platforms, technological interventions and field-level innovations are contributing to improved service delivery, stronger institutional mechanisms and more effective implementation of welfare initiatives, the Secretary said.
The Secretary said the Ministry expects the Summit to facilitate the participating States for a meaningful exchange of ideas and formulation of actionable strategies and encourage mutual learning among States and Union Territories, towards achieving the vision of an inclusive, equitable and empowered society.
He said the key outcomes and action plans, along with defined timelines for implementation, will be presented before the Hon’ble Prime Minister, Shri Narendra Modi, during the Valedictory Session.
The Hon’ble PM’s guidance is expected to provide renewed impetus to the collective resolve of the Centre and States and strengthen decisive, coordinated and time bound action towards achieving the agreed outcomes and advancing the vision of
Viksit Bharat@2047
, the Secretary said.
With the preparations complete, the Ministry looks forward to welcoming representatives from across the country for two days of constructive dialogue, shared learning and collective commitment towards a more inclusive and empowered India, Shri Pant concluded.
