title: Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas 2026 Celebrated Across the Country
subtitle:
Nation Celebrates Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas on the 151st Birth Anniversary of Dharti Aaba Bhagwan Birsa Munda

Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi joins main event at Gadchiroli, Maharashtra through video conferencing; inaugurates and lays foundation stones of 246 projects worth around ₹3,000 crore

Chief Ministers, Governors and Ministers lead State-level celebrations; over 25,000 events with more than 60 lakh participants held across 34 States and UTs during the Janjatiya Gaurav Pakhwada
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                17 NOV 2026 8:22PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Ministry of Tribal Affairs, together with State Governments and Union Territory Administrations, celebrated Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas across the country on 15 November 2026, marking the 151st birth anniversary of Dharti Aaba Bhagwan Birsa Munda. The day marked the culmination of the Janjatiya Gaurav Pakhwada, observed from 1 to 15 November 2026 with cultural, educational, welfare and outreach activities in tribal areas across the country.
The celebrations began in New Delhi with the Hon'ble President Droupadi Murmu, Vice President and Rajya Sabha chairman C. P. Radhakrishnan, Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla on Sunday paid floral tributes to Bhagwan Birsa Munda on his birth anniversary, observed as Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas, at Prerna Sthal in the Parliament premises. Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Law and Justice and Minister of State for Parliamentary Affairs Arjun Ram Meghwal, Members of Parliament and other distinguished dignitaries also joined the tribute ceremony.
Floral tributes were also paid at Ulihatu, Jharkhand, the birthplace of Bhagwan Birsa Munda. The National Tribal Pride March was ceremonially flagged off from Ulihatu, in Khunti district of Jharkhand, the birthplace of Bhagwan Birsa Munda, to mark his 151st birth anniversary and Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas.
The main national event was held at the District Sports Complex, Gadchiroli, Maharashtra, where the Hon'ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi joined through video conferencing. The programme was presided over by the Hon'ble Governor of Maharashtra Shri Jishnu Dev Varma, Union Minister of Tribal Affairs Shri Jual Oram, Chief Minister of Maharashtra Shri Devendra Fadnavis, Deputy Chief Ministers Shri Eknath Shinde and Smt. Sunetra Pawar, Minister of State for Tribal Affairs Shri Durgadas Uikey,  and various other dignitaries.
Floral tribute was paid at the statue of Bhagwan Birsa Munda on behalf of the Hon'ble Prime Minister. Earlier in the day, the Government of Maharashtra inaugurated 22 Ashram Schools and 51 hostels.
The Hon'ble Prime Minister inaugurated and laid the foundation stones of 246 projects worth around ₹3,000 crore across various States. Projects inaugurated include 38 Eklavya Model Residential Schools, 100 Multi-Purpose Centres under PM-JANMAN, the new building of the Tribal Research Institute in Arunachal Pradesh and the Ropuiliani Tribal Freedom Fighter Museum at Kelsih, Mizoram and many others. Foundation stones were laid for 19 Eklavya Model Residential Schools, 12 Tribal Multipurpose Marketing Centres, Ashram Schools and other projects under PM-JANMAN and Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan.
Addressing the gathering, the Prime Minister greeted citizens with ‘Johar’ and paid tribute to Bhagwan Birsa Munda and to the tribal heroes associated with Gadchiroli, including Raghoji Bhangre, Bhagoji Naik and Veer Baburao Shedmake. He said that Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas, first observed on 15 November 2021, has become a national festival, and that India is today remembering its heritage, history and heroes with indigenous self-respect. Recalling tribal struggles against colonial rule, from Tirot Sing in the Khasi Hills and Sidho-Kanho's Santhal revolution to Govind Guru's followers at Mangarh, Rani Gaidinliu, Tantya Bhil, Alluri Sitarama Raju and Rani Durgavati, he said that Bhagwan Birsa Munda's Ulgulan continues to inspire crores of Indians.
The Prime Minister said the day coincided with two major national achievements closely linked to tribal communities: nearly 50 crore citizens rising out of extreme poverty over the past 12–13 years, as reported by the World Bank, and the country becoming free from Naxalism and Maoist terror. He noted that more than ₹1 lakh crore has been allocated for PM-JANMAN and the Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan, so that families who received facilities last after Independence now receive them first. Expressing pride that the country's highest office is held by a daughter of the tribal community, President Smt. Droupadi Murmu, he urged citizens to draw inspiration from Bhagwan Birsa Munda and work towards a Viksit Bharat 2047, and to celebrate Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas every year with greater enthusiasm and on a larger scale.
States and Union Territories held State-level programmes led by Chief Ministers, Governors and Ministers. In Arunachal Pradesh, Chief Minister Shri Pema Khandu attended the inauguration of the new Tribal Research Institute building at Lobi, Itanagar, and in Mizoram, Chief Minister Shri Lalduhoma attended the inauguration of the Ropuiliani Tribal Freedom Fighter Museum. Chief Minister Shri Vishnu Deo Sai led the State-level programme at Raigarh, Chhattisgarh; Chief Minister Dr. Pramod Sawant attended the Adivasi Kala Samagam at Canacona, Goa, with around 15,000 participants; and Chief Minister Shri Mohan Majhi attended the mega event at Malkangiri, Odisha. In Gujarat, Chief Minister Shri Bhupendra Patel led the celebrations at Chhota Udepur with around 25,000 participants and Deputy Chief Minister Shri Harsh Sanghavi at Valsad, as part of 86 programmes held across the State. Chief Minister Shri Pushkar Singh Dhami led the main programme at Parade Ground, Dehradun, with Union Minister of State Shri Ajay Tamta, while Chief Minister Shri Omar Abdullah attended the commemoration at Mendhar, Jammu and Kashmir. In Rajasthan, Chief Minister Shri Bhajan Lal Sharma joined floral tributes held across Tribal Area Development offices, Ashram hostels and EMRS. The Chief Minister of Manipur opened the State-level Tribal Cultural Festival at Imphal, which also marked the close of the second edition of the Tribal Frames National Tribal Film Festival.
The Hon'ble Governor of Tripura attended the felicitation-cum-cultural programme at the Tripura State Academy of Tribal Culture, Agartala. In Assam, the celebration at Shilpgram, Guwahati, featured the Janjatiya Gaurav Award for five tribal achievers, grants to tribal homestay beneficiaries and a workshop on tribal land rights and the Forest Rights Act, 2006. Karnataka held its State-level event at the Karnataka State Open University, Mysuru, in the presence of the State Minister for ST Welfare, and Uttar Pradesh held floral tributes in all 75 districts, with the State Minister for Social Welfare Shri Asim Arun attending the event at Kannauj. In Sikkim, State Minister Shri Samdup Lepcha attended a programme showcasing the State's tribal heritage, while in Andaman and Nicobar Islands, members of the Onge, Great Andamanese and Nicobarese communities watched the Prime Minister's address live and received Ayushman cards. Ladakh inaugurated a Birsa Van at the Kargil campus of the University of Ladakh, and Jharkhand, Kerala, Himachal Pradesh and other States held floral tributes, award ceremonies, seminars and cultural programmes.
During the Pakhwada, State Tribal Research Institutes, Tribal Welfare Departments and district administrations organised over 25,000 events across 34 States and Union Territories, with the participation of more than 60 lakh people. The activities included cultural festivals, exhibitions, competitions in schools, colleges, EMRS and hostels, scholarship and Aadhaar camps, health and nutrition camps for PVTGs at PM-JANMAN Multi-Purpose Centres, legal literacy camps on forest rights, and community service drives under the Dharti Aaba Janbhagidari Abhiyan. Jammu and Kashmir, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Telangana and Karnataka recorded the highest number of events and participants.
Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas was declared by the Union Cabinet in 2021 to honour the contribution of tribal freedom fighters and tribal communities to the nation. Building on Janjatiya Gaurav Varsh 2024–25, which marked the 150th birth anniversary of Bhagwan Birsa Munda with over 2 lakh events and more than 3.7 crore participants, this year's celebrations continued to bring tribal heritage, achievements and development to the centre of national attention.

title: Cabinet Secretary launches Karmayogi Sankalpa at NITI Aayog’s National Workshop on “Leadership as a Mission”
subtitle: Civil servants across the country to record commitments to specific changes in their leadership practice on the iGOT Karmayogi platform
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                17 NOV 2026 9:25PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Dr. T.V. Somanathan, Cabinet Secretary, today launched the Karmayogi Sankalpa on the iGOT Karmayogi platform at the valedictory session of the National Workshop on “Leadership as a Mission”, organised by NITI Aayog at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi. The workshop is the first in a series of five National Workshops being organised by NITI Aayog on the completion of twenty-five years of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi as Head of Government.
Under the Karmayogi Sankalpa, each civil servant records one commitment to a specific change in their own leadership practice. The commitment sets out where the officer will act, the leadership attributes the officer will build, the change that citizens will see, and the action the officer will take. Participants at Bharat Mandapam and officers joining through the iGOT Karmayogi platform recorded their commitments at the time of the launch. The commitments of government officers will be followed up by Karmayogi Bharat. The Sankalpa will be taken forward through Ministries, State Governments and training institutions, with a target of 25,000 commitments to be recorded on the platform by 25 December 2026, which is observed as Good Governance Day.
The day opened with the
inaugural keynote address by Dr. P.K. Mishra, Principal Secretary to the Prime Minister,
followed by first-hand accounts on the reconstruction of Kutch after the 2001 earthquake, the response to Covid-19, Lakhpati Didi and the opening up of the space economy. In the Case Clinic, each group examined one decision from its assigned episode, considering what public purpose required in the decision, what stood against it, and how the decision was held to its purpose through implementation.
A panel discussion on “Leadership for Viksit Bharat” was
moderated by Shri B.V.R. Subrahmanyam, former Chief Executive Officer, NITI Aayog
. The panelists were Shri Arvind Kumar Sharma, Cabinet Minister for Urban Development and Energy, Government of Uttar Pradesh, Prof. Vishal Gupta, Indian Institute of Management Ahmedabad, Ms. Debjani Ghosh, former President, NASSCOM and Distinguished Fellow, NITI Aayog, and Ms. Narayani Bhatia, Joint Magistrate, Hardoi, Uttar Pradesh.
The panelists shared their thoughts on Hon’ble Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s leadership principles and their relevance to achieving the vision of Viksit Bharat 2047.
Shri Arvind Kumar Sharma
highlighted the paradigm shift in governance during the Prime Minister’s tenure as Chief Minister of Gujarat, emphasizing his ability to create new processes, build institution and human resource capacity and placing local communities at the centre of development.
Prof. Vishal Gupta
underscored the Prime Minister’s ability to inspire belief in ambitious goals. He stressed that political will must go hand in hand with administrative reforms and highlighted
Seva Bhav
as a defining principle of leadership.
Ms. Debjani Ghosh
emphasized that technology must ultimately be measured by its impact on people and society. She called for placing human-centricity at the heart of AI and technological advancement, ensuring that innovation translates into meaningful societal change.
Ms. Narayani Bhatia
highlighted the Prime Minister’s lateral thinking, ability to identify interconnected opportunities. She particularly emphasised his practice of deep listening and empathy, noting that giving people, including young bureaucrats, the space to share their perspectives is one of the most valuable qualities of his leadership.
In the Application Clinic, government officers applied the learnings from the Case Clinic to live leadership challenges from the current postings of participating officers.
At the valedictory session,
Dr. R. Balasubramaniam, Member, NITI Aayog
, presented a recap of the day’s proceedings. Additionally, various groups presented their application for challenges related to ASR SAATHI – Safe Antenatal Assistance aimed at tracking and sustaining maternal care across remote tribal habitations; operationalizing closed-loop referral pathways to deliver universal health coverage for non-communicable diseases; making every Saras Mela deliver year-round buyer commitments so SHG enterprises can sustain Lakhpati Didi incomes; and ensuring the initial and long-term functionality of grey water management assets under SBM-G.
In his closing remarks, Dr. T.V. Somanathan, Cabinet Secretary,
said that
“Leadership lessons can be studied through academic courses and research, but the most valuable lessons come from observing and working with accomplished leaders. Drawing upon his experience of working with leaders like the Hon’ble Prime Minister Narendra Modi, he highlighted key administrative leadership practices that civil servants can adopt. Karmayogi Sankalpa will carry the learning of the workshop into the field. Dr. Somanathan emphasised that effective leadership is best understood through the experience of accomplished leaders and highlighted the importance of learning from their administrative skills.
He added that effective administrative leadership is about translating vision into measurable outcomes through purposeful questioning, active listening, decisive decision-making, accountability and adherence to due process.
The analysis of the groups will be developed by case writers into case studies, which will be published on the iGOT Karmayogi platform for use by civil servants and training institutions. The application plans prepared by every group and the commitments recorded under the Karmayogi Sankalpa will carry the learning of the workshop into the field. The next National Workshop in the series, on “Governance as Delivery” will be held in January 2027. The workshop concluded with a
vote of thanks by Shri Anurag Jain, Chief Executive Officer, NITI Aayog
.

title: NITI Aayog holds first National Workshop on “Leadership as a Mission” on the completion of 25 years of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi as Head of Government
subtitle: Dr. P.K. Mishra, Principal Secretary to the Prime Minister, delivers inaugural keynote address at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                17 NOV 2026 2:46PM by PIB Delhi
content:
NITI Aayog organised the National Workshop on “Leadership as Mission” at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi today, to draw on the learnings from the twenty-five years of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi as Head of Government. The Prime Minister assumed office as Chief Minister of Gujarat in October 2001 and as Prime Minister of India in May 2014 and has led the Government at the State and the Union levels without a break since then. Throughout this period, he has held public office as a mission of service. His description of himself as the Pradhan Sevak places the citizen at the centre of every office of government, and the principles of Antyodaya, Jan Bhagidari and Sabka Saath, Sabka Vikas, Sabka Vishwas, Sabka Prayas have guided the direction of governance at both levels.
The workshop is the first in a series of five National Workshops. The deliberations and first-hand experiences shared during the series will be developed into case studies and learning material for civil services training institutes, educational institutions and universities. Over the course of the series, the learning from these twenty-five years will also be taken forward through research and teaching material that sets out directions for policy and administration in the years leading up to Viksit Bharat @2047.
More than 900 participants attended the workshop, of whom 250 took part directly in the deliberations. The participants included Secretaries and senior officers of the Union and State Governments, District Collectors of Aspirational Districts, students of educational institutions and universities, and community partners and beneficiaries of national flagship schemes. The proceedings are also streamed on the iGOT Karmayogi platform and at Central and State Administrative Training Institutes, enabling officers from across the country to participate in the programme.
The workshop commenced with the National Song and the National Anthem followed by welcome address by
Shri Anurag Jain, Chief Executive Officer, NITI Aayog
.
He highlighted that the objective of this workshop is to document the learnings from 25 years of leadership of the Hon’ble Prime Minister and translate them into institutional knowledge for the future.
He outlined four key lessons from the leadership journey. First, purpose must take precedence over hierarchical position, shifting the focus from individual leadership to a shared collective mission. Second, service must replace command, with governance centred on reaching the last person in the queue. Third, intrinsic conviction builds resilience, enabling adversity to become an opportunity for societal transformation. And fourth, true empowerment must outlive individual leadership through strong institutions, capable teams and sustainable systems.
Shri Ashok Kumar Lahiri, Vice Chairman, NITI Aayog,
delivered the opening remarks. He said, “
The role of strong political and administrative leadership is crucial in driving India's development journey. The transformational vision of our Hon’ble Prime Minister, marks a significant shift in India's national aspiration to become Viksit by 2047,
reflecting the country’s transition towards a developed, prosperous and globally competitive nation.”
He highlighted NITI Aayog's integrated roadmap for realising this ambition of building a USD 30-40 trillion economy by 2047, with a per capita income of USD 15,000-18,000, supported by sustained annual real GDP growth of 7-10%.
Delivering the inaugural keynote address,
Dr. P. K. Mishra, Principal Secretary to the Prime Minister,
said that
“India’s governance journey has been marked by defining milestones that demonstrate the power of decisive leadership and the ability to translate vision into action. From swift response to the 2001 Kutch earthquake to the country’s coordinated response to the COVID-19 pandemic, from expanding India’s footprint in the global space economy to the transformative impact of Lakhpati Didi initiative, these actions reflect how strong political will, responsive administration and mission-driven governance can bring about meaningful change in people’s lives.”
Shri Uday Kotak, Founder, Kotak Mahindra Bank,
said that
“The leadership of Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, both as Chief Minister of Gujarat and subsequently as Prime Minister of India, has consistently recognised entrepreneurship as a key driver of economic growth and nation-building. The institutionalisation of support systems, strengthening of financial and entrepreneurial ecosystems, and the emergence of a vibrant start-up landscape reflect this commitment.”
Dr. R. Balasubramaniam, Member, NITI Aayog
, explained the design and structure of the workshop.
He stated that the workshop approaches leadership through the decisions and actions in which it becomes visible, with the day’s proceedings structured to move from experience to analysis and from analysis to practice. The proceedings followed five stages: Learn, Analyse, Reflect, Apply and Commit under which participants learnt from first-hand accounts of significant decisions, analysed them through deliberations involving government, academia and citizens, reflected on enduring practices of public leadership, applied the learning to challenges in their own work and committed to specific changes in their leadership practices. He added that the workshop seeks to build an Indian body of knowledge on public leadership, drawing on Indian decisions and institutions, which will shape the way civil servants are trained and the way they lead in the years towards Viksit Bharat 2047.
During the Leadership Moments session, four speakers shared first-hand accounts of key moments and the leadership lessons emerging from them.
Shri Rajeev Topno, Additional Chief Secretary and Principal Secretary, Health and Family Welfare Department, Government of Gujarat,
spoke on the reconstruction of Kutch following the 2001 earthquake. He highlighted that,
Kutch 2001 was not merely a story of restoring normalcy, it was a story of creating a new normal through Jan Bhagidari, institutional strength and collective resolve. The experience highlighted four key pillars of effective governance, clarity and decisiveness in vision, solidarity and commitment, people’s participation with State support, and strong institution building.
Ms. Preeti Sudan, former Union Health Secretary and former Chairman, UPSC and former Member, Independent Panel for Pandemic Preparedness and Response,
emphasised
that under the leadership of Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, India’s COVID-19 response evolved from a whole-of-government approach into a whole-of-society movement. With the safety of doctors, nurses and frontline warriors prioritised, technology as its backbone, and Jan Andolan driving public participation, India mounted a coordinated response. Through Vaccine Maitri, the country further extended its commitment to global solidarity, supplying approximately 300 million vaccine doses to over 100 countries.
Shri Shailesh Kumar Singh, former Secretary, Ministry of Rural Development
,
Government of India
said that “
The Lakhpati Didi initiative is an example of how a vision can be translated into action at an unprecedented scale. The Hon’ble Prime Minister recognised rural women as entrepreneurs, producers and service providers, giving the initiative a clear and ambitious goal. Lakhpati Didi initiative goes beyond income generation, it is about fostering economic independence, dignity and recognition for women within their families and society. That, to me, is its larger purpose.”
Dr. S. Somanath, former Chairman, ISRO and former Secretary, Department of Space, Government of India,
highlighted
how liberalised FDI norms have opened new avenues for private sector participation, enabling space to emerge as a significant contributor to the economy. He emphasized that ISRO is playing a crucial role in facilitating this transition by extending its expertise, infrastructure and facilities to private players. Looking ahead, India’s Space Vision 2047, will further advance our scientific capabilities and strengthen India's position as a global space power.
Following the session, participants took part in the Case Clinic, where each group examined a specific decision from its assigned episode. Each group comprised of government officers, community partners and students, and was guided by a case writer trained under the Amrit Gyaan Kosh initiative of the Capacity Building Commission. The group deliberations, together with the first-hand accounts shared by the speakers, will be developed into case studies by the Capacity Building Commission and made available on the iGOT Karmayogi platform for use by civil servants, training institutions and universities.
Later in the day, a panel discussion on “Leadership for Viksit Bharat” will be held and government officers will take part in the Application Clinic. Dr. T.V. Somanathan, Cabinet Secretary, will launch the Karmayogi Sankalpa and deliver the closing remarks.

title: Naturopathy: Natural Healing for a Healthy India
subtitle: Treatment, Training, Research and Care Across the Country
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                17 NOV 2026 10:03AM by PIB Delhi
content:
Naturopathy is a drug-free, cost-effective system that helps the body heal itself through diet, fasting, water, mud, massage and natural living. India observes National Naturopathy Day on 18 November, and the 9th edition will be held at Nagamangala, Karnataka, under the theme ‘Prakrutik Chikitsa, Swasth Bharat’. The National Institute of Naturopathy, Pune, runs Nisarg Gram, a 250-bedded naturopathy hospital with the first Bachelor of Naturopathy and Yogic Sciences (BNYS) college under the Central Government.
Healing with Nature
Naturopathy rests on a simple idea: the body has the power to heal itself. Rooted in the healing wisdom of many cultures, it is a cost-effective, drug-free approach that uses natural materials for health care and healthy living. It works by boosting the body’s own vitality, with the help of the five elements of nature: earth, water, air, fire and ether.
Naturopathy is a system of natural treatment and also a way of life. It calls for a “Return to Nature”: simple eating and living habits, and a life in harmony with oneself, society and the environment. It has the potential to promote health, prevent illness, cure it and help in recovery.
Treatments in Naturopathy
A naturopath treats with what nature provides: fasting and diet, hydrotherapy (treatment with water), mud packs, cold packs, baths and massages. At Nisarg Gram, the Pune campus of the National Institute of Naturopathy, treatment sections also offer magnetotherapy (treatment with magnets), chromotherapy (colour therapy) and physiotherapy, along with a yoga hall and a Saatvik diet centre.
Where Naturopathy Helps
Naturopathy is reported to be effective in chronic, allergic, autoimmune, degenerative and stress-related disorders. Its emphasis on nutrition, natural therapies and lifestyle change has found new relevance as attention grows to lifestyle-related disorders, obesity, stress and healthy ageing. A Healthy diet, physical activity, adequate rest and stress management can support preventive healthcare across age groups.
Naturopathy and Yoga in India
In India, naturopathy goes hand in hand with yoga. In the words of the National Institute of Naturopathy, Indian naturopathy includes yoga along with ancient Indian concepts such as a ‘Panchabhuta-based understanding of health and disease’, the Panchabhuta being the five elements of nature named above. Over time, it has grown into a holistic system that treats and prevents disease and teaches people to live a healthy life close to nature. Yoga and Naturopathy are listed together among the Ayush systems, along with Ayurveda, Unani, Siddha, Sowa Rigpa and Homoeopathy. At the National Conference on Naturopathy 2026, the Ministry of Ayush reiterated that Yoga and Naturopathy complement each other. The Government has built a full system around this pairing: a degree that joins naturopathy with yogic sciences; a research council for both, the Central Council for Research in Yoga and Naturopathy (CCRYN); central registration of practitioners; and the country’s first national naturopathy hospital.
9th National Naturopathy Day: Prakrutik Chikitsa, Swasth Bharat
The 9th National Naturopathy Day will be observed on 18 November 2026 at the Central Research Institute of Yoga and Naturopathy (CRIYN), Nagamangala, Karnataka. Its theme, ‘Prakrutik Chikitsa, Swasth Bharat’, puts prevention first: good diet, physical activity, yoga and stress management, with a focus on preventing obesity. The observance aligns with the Prime Minister’s vision of a Fit and Healthy India. Shri Prataprao Jadhav, Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Ayush and Minister of State for Health and Family Welfare, said:
“Naturopathy encourages us to recognise the close relationship between lifestyle, nature and overall health. Our emphasis is on strengthening its scientific foundation through credible research, quality education and responsible integration with conventional healthcare.”
Mahatma Gandhi and the Origin of Naturopathy Day
Naturopathy Day honours a commitment Mahatma Gandhi made to nature cure. On 18 November 1945, he became the Lifetime Chairman of the All India Nature Cure Foundation Trust in Pune and signed its deed. The Ministry of Ayush declared the date to be observed every year as Naturopathy Day, beginning in 2018. Gandhi is considered the founding figure of naturopathy in India. In 1946, he led a nature cure campaign at Uruli Kanchan, a village near Pune. Writing that year, he said:
“I hold that where the rules of personal, domestic and public sanitation are strictly observed and due care is taken in the matter of diet and exercise, there should be no occasion for illness or disease. Where there is absolute purity, inner and outer, illness becomes impossible.
If the village people could but understand this, they would not need doctors, Hakims or Vaidyas.” (Harijan, 26 May 1946)
National Institute of Naturopathy and Nisarg Gram
The National Institute of Naturopathy (NIN), Pune, came into existence on 22 December 1986, at the nature cure centre handed over to the Government of India on 17 March 1975. Its home, “Bapu Bhavan”, is named after Mahatma Gandhi. NIN is an autonomous body under the Ministry of Ayush, and its Governing Body is headed by the Union Minister of Ayush. NIN works to:
provide and encourage facilities for standardisation and dissemination of existing knowledge in naturopathy and yoga;
promote quality training and education in naturopathy and yoga by establishing a Nature Cure University;
conduct, facilitate and encourage research in all aspects of human health; and
establish a living memorial to Mahatma Gandhi.
NIN runs special Out-Patient Department (OPD) clinics for common needs: a Maternal Care OPD for health before and after childbirth, a Diabetes OPD that works through diet, yoga and lifestyle change, and a Mind-Body Medicine OPD that uses yoga, meditation and relaxation for stress and anxiety.
Nisarg Gram
On 25 February 2024, Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi inaugurated ‘Nisarg Gram’, the new campus of NIN in Pune. Spread over 25 acres and built at a cost of Rs. 213.55 crore, it has a 250-bedded hospital, a centre for research and extension services, and a Naturopathy Medical College for undergraduate, postgraduate and paramedical courses. It is the first national naturopathy hospital, where lifestyle-related metabolic disorders can be addressed through natural therapies.
Nisarg Gram at a Glance
Campus:
25 acres, Yewalewadi, Pune
Cost:
Rs. 213.55 crore
Hospital:
250 beds, the first national naturopathy hospital
College:
Naturopathy Medical College, with 100 BNYS seats in 2026-27
Facilities:
yoga hall, Saatvik diet centre, hydrotherapy, magnetotherapy, chromotherapy, massage and physiotherapy
Reaching Tribal Communities
With the help of the Tribal Development Department, Government of Maharashtra, NIN has set up Nisarg Arogya Sadhana Kendra, a full-fledged yoga and naturopathy hospital for tribal people at Gohe (Budruk), Ambegaon taluka, Pune district. The unit has 20 beds, separate wards for men and women, a yoga hall and a diet centre. It aims to meet the nutritional needs of the community through locally available resources and to offer a self-sustaining model of health care through natural therapies. The unit also serves as a training centre where tribal youth learn to bring the skills of naturopathy and yoga into their own health practices. Its Treatment Assistant Training Course has an admission capacity of 40 tribal students a year.
Naturopathy calls for a life in harmony with nature. That is common ground with tribal communities, whose knowledge and harmony with nature are recognised each year on Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas, observed on 15 November, the birth anniversary of Bhagwan Birsa Munda. The Government is building on this ground. On 16 January 2026, the Ministry of Tribal Affairs held a national capacity-building programme for tribal healers in Hyderabad, in collaboration with the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, the Indian Council of Medical Research and the Ministry of Ayush, to engage the healers as community-level partners in health outreach in tribal areas. The Ministry has set an indicative national target to enable the recognition of one lakh tribal healers. During Janjatiya Gaurav Pakhwada 2026, a capacity building conclave in Hyderabad on 1 and 2 November brought together around 1,500 traditional healers from 9 States and Union Territories for training.
Training the Next Generation of Naturopaths
A growing system needs trained doctors, and the Government has built a clear path for them.
The BNYS Degree
NIN is the first Central Government institution in the country to offer the Bachelor of Naturopathy and Yogic Sciences (BNYS) programme in affiliation with a Central University, Shri Lal Bahadur Shastri National Sanskrit University, New Delhi. A BNYS student lives on campus for 5½ years: 4½ years of academic and clinical training, followed by a one-year Compulsory Rotatory Residential Internship. For the academic session 2026-27, 100 seats are offered at Nisarg Gram, with classes set to begin on 30 November 2026.
Across the country, 71 naturopathy undergraduate colleges had an admission capacity of 5,214 students while 6 postgraduate colleges had a capacity of 144 students, as on 1 April 2024. As on 1 January 2024, 5,083 naturopathy practitioners were registered with State Boards and Councils.
Central Registration
The Naturopathy Registration Board (NRB), constituted by the Ministry of Ayush under the aegis of NIN, provides central registration to naturopathy practitioners and accredits naturopathy institutions and hospitals. BNYS graduates from universities recognised by the University Grants Commission can apply for its Central Registration Certificate.
Courses for Self-Care
NIN also runs short skill development courses. Courses in acupressure, naturopathy and naturopathy cooking are mostly for self-help, so that people can care for their own health and that of their families, under the motto of “Self Health Reliance”. Courses in massage, fitness training and yoga help people support themselves professionally.
Building the Evidence: Research and New Hospitals
Research gives naturopathy its scientific footing. Vaidya Rajesh Kotecha, Secretary, Ministry of Ayush, said:
“Scientific validation is essential for strengthening the credibility and wider application of naturopathy. Through CCRYN and other institutions, we are encouraging systematic research, clinical evaluation and collaboration so that naturopathic practices can be assessed through appropriate scientific methods and translated into responsible healthcare approaches.”
Research Council, Institutes and Hospitals
The Central Council for Research in Yoga and Naturopathy (CCRYN), fully funded by the Ministry of Ayush, has been engaged in research, promotion and development in yoga and naturopathy since 1978. The Council has 22 units across India. The Ministry’s five research councils together published 653 research papers during 2025-26.
India now has 200-bed Yoga and Naturopathy hospitals at Jhajjar in Haryana and Nagamangala in Karnataka, along with postgraduate institutes for Yoga and Naturopathy education and research. The CRIYN at Jhajjar, an apex research and education facility built on 19 acres for Rs. 63.88 crore, was inaugurated by the Prime Minister on 25 February 2024, the same day as Nisarg Gram. In 2024, the Prime Minister also laid the foundation stones of two more CRIYNs, at Khorda in Odisha and Raipur in Chhattisgarh. As of 1 April 2024, Naturopathy care is available in 35 hospitals with 1,663 beds and in 95 dispensaries across the country.
The National Institute of Naturopathy (NIN) also has a dedicated Research Department and an Institutional Ethics Committee registered with the Department of Health Research. It runs research methodology workshops, Good Clinical Practice training, observational studies, systematic reviews and collaborative research. Its ongoing in-house studies look at different methods of fasting, hip baths and wet sheet packs, the effect of sun exposure on type 2 diabetes, an integrated naturopathy and yoga programme and its effect on gut microbiota (the microbes that live in the gut), and naturopathy and yoga for osteoarthritis of the knee.
India’s Traditional Systems and the World
India is drawing more patients from abroad. The number of international patients visiting India, for all kinds of care rose from 1,82,945 in 2020 to 6,44,387 in 2024, and Yoga, Ayurveda and wellness-based therapies have emerged as major contributors to this growth. India’s traditional systems, Ayurveda, Yoga, Naturopathy, Unani, Siddha and Homoeopathy, are increasingly being chosen by international patients for the management of chronic diseases, lifestyle disorders, rehabilitation and wellness programmes.
India’s wellness tourism centres on preventive and holistic well-being through traditional systems such as Yoga, Ayurveda and Naturopathy. To make such care easier to reach, the Government introduced a dedicated Ayush Visa on 27 July 2023 for foreign nationals and their attendants seeking treatment under Ayush systems. The Prime Minister had announced the visa at the Global Ayush Investment and Innovation Summit in Gandhinagar in April 2022. It is part of India’s roadmap for the Heal in India initiative, which promotes India as a destination for medical value travel. Ayush Centres will also form part of five proposed Regional Medical Value Tourism Hubs announced in the Union Budget in February 2026, combining advanced medical treatment with traditional therapies, wellness services and rehabilitation.
Carrying Nature Cure Forward
Naturopathy works with simple means: good food, rest, movement and the healing power of nature. India has given this system a national institute and the first national naturopathy hospital, a degree under a Central University, research institutes and hospitals, central registration, and Ayush care at health centres across the country. On 18 November 2026, as the 9th National Naturopathy Day is observed at Nagamangala, the focus is on good diet, physical activity, yoga and healthy living for every age, under the vision of ‘Prakrutik Chikitsa, Swasth Bharat’.

title: India's Solar Growth Enters a New Era
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                17 NOV 2026 9:42AM by PIB Delhi
content:
India’s solar energy sector has expanded significantly over the past decade, emerging as a key driver of the country’s energy transition. Growth in installed capacity, domestic manufacturing and distributed solar adoption reflects the sector’s expanding reach. Policy support, infrastructure development and citizen participation are accelerating this transformation. Solar power is strengthening energy security, supporting economic development and advancing climate action. These developments formed part of the broader discussions at the Bharat Renewable Energy Summit & Expo (BRESE) 2026, held in New Delhi from 2–5 November.
India's Solar Rise
A decade ago, solar power occupied only a small place in India's electricity mix. Today, it forms the largest share of the country's renewable energy capacity. From an installed capacity of
2.82 GW in 2014
, the sector has expanded approximately 62 fold, reaching
~
175 GW till 31 October 2026
.
This transformation is driven by policy support, infrastructure development, manufacturing expansion, and citizen participation. Initiatives such as solar parks, rooftop systems, and solarised agricultural pumps are accelerating deployment across the country.  India’s expanding renewable energy sector was in focus at the Bharat Renewable Energy Summit & Expo (BRESE) 2026. The event brought together global stakeholders to advance cooperation, investment and innovation in clean energy.
The
Bharat Renewable Energy Summit & Expo (BRESE) 2026
was organised from 2–5 November at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi. Held under the theme
‘Invest. Innovate. Inspire.’
,
it brought together
participants from over 130 countries,
including policymakers, industry leaders, investors and researchers. Co-located with the
9th International Solar Alliance (ISA) Assembly and the 4th International Conference on Green Hydrogen
, the Summit hosted high-level discussions and ministerial meetings. It also facilitated business engagements and featured an exhibition involving over 400 organisations. 13 states participated as Partner States, showcasing their renewable energy potential and investment opportunities. The Summit also recognised winners of the
Bharat Renewable Energy Hackathon 2026
, featuring solutions to ten real-world renewable energy challenges.
India's solar momentum has translated into measurable outcomes. The country has added 37 GW of solar capacity in 2025, surpassing the United States in annual additions. India has also emerged as the
world's second-largest solar growth market
, underlining its growing role in the global clean energy transition.
A Decade of Solar Expansion
A strong policy framework laid the foundation for India's solar expansion. Key initiatives included the National Solar Mission (2010), the Solar Parks Scheme, the Green Energy Corridor Programme, and competitive bidding. Together, they accelerated large-scale solar deployment.
Solar Capacity Across India
Solar deployment spans diverse geographies and climatic zones. Rajasthan, Gujarat, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, and Maharashtra account for a significant share of installed capacity.
Large solar projects
contribute
133 GW
(including solar component of hybrid projects)
of installed capacity
. Some of the large solar projects include the
Bhadla Solar Park (Rajasthan), Pavagada Solar Park (Karnataka), Ananthapuramu & Kurnool Solar Parks (Andhra Pradesh), and Rewa Ultra Mega Solar Park (Madhya Pradesh).
Rooftop solar systems connected to the electricity grid contribute another
34.97 GW
. The remaining capacity comes from off-grid solar systems.
Hybrid projects combine solar power with battery storage or other power sources, while Off-grid systems provide electricity in areas not connected to the grid.
Record Growth in Recent Years
India has recorded significant additions to solar and non-fossil fuel capacity in recent years, reflecting its expanding clean energy transition.
India added
44.61 GW
of solar capacity in the last FY 2025-26, nearly double the
23.83 GW
added in FY 2024–25. In the current FY 2026-27, already 24.29 GW of solar capacity, following the same pace as of previous FY.
Solar module manufacturing capacity increased from
2.3 GW in 2014
to about
172 GW
as of 31 March 2026. It further increased to 192 GW by June 2026.
Total non-fossil fuel capacity reached 308.03 GW as of 30 September 2026, including 299.25 GW of renewable energy capacity and 8.78 GW of nuclear power capacity.
Highest-ever annual addition of non-fossil fuel capacity recorded at
55.29 GW
in FY 2025-26.
On 29 July 2025, renewable energy sources met
51.5%
of India's electricity demand, the highest monthly share recorded so far.
Policy Architecture Behind the Solar
Expansion
A stable policy framework, competitive bidding mechanisms, and long-term targets have helped create a conducive environment for large-scale solar deployment. A set of mutually reinforcing measures has supported India's solar expansion. These can be broadly grouped into five pillars:
Creating Vision: Climate Commitments and Long-Term Targets
At COP26 in Glasgow, India announced the Panchamrit goals, which include 500 GW of non-fossil fuel capacity by 2030 and net-zero emissions by 2070. These commitments were reflected in India's updated Nationally Determined Contributions under the Paris Agreement.
Complementing these efforts,
Mission LiFE (Lifestyle for Environment)
promotes sustainable consumption and encourages citizens to adopt environmentally conscious practices.
Creating Demand: National Missions and Renewable Purchase Obligations
Strong and sustained demand has been central to India's solar growth. The National Solar Mission established long-term capacity targets and provided an early impetus to solar deployment.
Renewable Purchase Obligations (RPOs)
require electricity distribution companies and other obligated entities to procure a specified share of their electricity from renewable sources. RPOs provide long-term market certainty for developers and investors while encouraging greater renewable energy adoption. The RPO trajectory has been notified through
2029–30
, with the target for 2026–27, set at
35.95 per cent
.
Demand has also expanded beyond utilities and large developers
. PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana
is encouraging households to adopt rooftop solar systems. Meanwhile,
Pradhan Mantri Kisan Urja Suraksha evam Utthaan Mahabhiyan
(PM-KUSUM)
is supporting the adoption of solar pumps and feeder solarisation in the agriculture sector. Together, these initiatives are expanding the market for solar energy and strengthening participation across consumers, farmers, businesses, and power utilities.
Lowering Costs: Competitive Bidding and Tariff Discovery
One of the most significant developments in solar sector has been the
decline in power tariffs over the past decade
. This was driven by bidding through the
e-Reverse Auction mechanism
, where developers compete to supply electricity at the lowest tariff.
Procurement agencies such as the
Solar Energy Corporation of India (SECI)
have played a key role in scaling this transparent tariff discovery mechanism. As more developers participated, the tariffs declined from around
₹18 per unit in 2010 to a record-low of ₹1.99 per unit.
This was achieved by the Gujarat Urja Vikas Nigam Ltd (GUVNL) in 2020.
This made solar power more affordable and accelerated its adoption across India.
The decline in tariffs has made solar power increasingly affordable. As a result, India has emerged as one of the world's lowest-cost solar power markets. In 2025, the Levelised Cost of Electricity (LCOE) from utility-scale solar PV stood at USD 35 per MWh, well below the global average of USD 44 per MWh.
Enabling Infrastructure
The government launched the
Solar Parks Scheme
to provide developers with ready access to land and supporting infrastructure. The scheme was initially launched with a target of 20 GW and later expanded to 40 GW in 2017. As of October 2026,
56 solar parks with a combined sanctioned capacity of 39,461 MW
have been approved across the country.

Bhadla Solar Park: From Desert Landscape to Clean Energy Hub
Located in Rajasthan's arid Bhadla region, the park has transformed vast stretches of barren land into one of the world's largest solar power complexes. Development began in

Spread across nearly

Beyond its scale, Bhadla showcases the solar park model in action. Common infrastructure, including land preparation and transmission facilities, enabled rapid project development and attracted significant private investment. Competitive bidding at the park also contributed to some of India's lowest solar tariffs, helping make solar energy more affordable.
Supporting the Solar Parks Scheme, the
Green Energy Corridor (GEC) Programme
aims to facilitate the transfer of power from RE-rich areas to demand centres across the country. The initiative strengthens transmission networks and supports the seamless integration of renewable energy into the electricity grid.
As of February 2026, the programme had enabled the evacuation of 24,567.8 MW of renewable energy through strengthened transmission networks. Green Energy Corridor projects across ten states are planned to support the evacuation of around 44 GW of renewable energy. These projects will also strengthen the integration of renewable energy into the national grid.
Floating Solar and Energy Storage
The Government approved the
Pradhan Mantri Surya Sarovar Yojana (PM-SSY)
on 31 July 2026. The scheme aims to support
5,000 MW
of Floating Solar Photovoltaic (FSPV) projects with co-located Energy Storage Systems (ESS). The ESS with a minimum storage capacity of
two hours
(10,000 MWh)
will further help states manage peak demand. By utilising existing reservoirs and industrial ponds, the scheme will reduce pressure on scarce land resources. It will also improve
grid reliability
through integrated energy storage. With an outlay of
₹5,070 crore
, the scheme will be implemented from
FY 2026– 27 to FY 2030– 31
.
The scheme is based on an assessment by the
National Institute of Solar Energy (NISE)
. The assessment estimates a
floating solar potential of about 102.18 GWp
across India's reservoirs and suitable inland water bodies. The scheme is expected to reduce
around 10 million tonnes of CO₂ emissions
annually. It will generate
16,000–17,000 full-time equivalent jobs
. It will also promote domestic manufacturing of floatation systems, PV cells, modules and energy storage systems. All
States and Union Territories
will be eligible to benefit through this scheme. The initiative will increase India's floating solar capacity by
5,000 MW
, from the current level of around
800 MW
.
Supporting Manufacturing
The Government has introduced measures to strengthen domestic solar manufacturing and reduce import dependence.
Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme for High-Efficiency Solar PV Modules
Launched in 2021 with an initial outlay of ₹4,500 crore, the PLI Scheme for High-Efficiency Solar PV Modules was expanded in 2022 with an additional ₹19,500 crore. The scheme promotes domestic manufacturing, reduces import dependence, and encourages value addition across the solar value chain. By October 2024, the scheme had attracted investments of around
₹35,000 crore
. It had also generated direct employment for about
10,000 people
.
Approved List of Models and Manufacturers (ALMM)
Introduced in
2019
, ALMM is a quality assurance framework for solar PV modules and cells. It ensures that solar equipment used in eligible projects meet specified quality and performance standards. Only manufacturers and models included in the approved lists are eligible for specified government-supported and competitively bid solar projects. The framework also promotes domestic manufacturing by encouraging the use of approved products.
Together, the PLI Scheme and ALMM have strengthened India's domestic solar manufacturing ecosystem. They have supported greater self-reliance while enabling rapid expansion of solar deployment. The framework also provides greater confidence to consumers and project developers by ensuring the use of approved solar equipment.
Taking Solar to Every Household and Farm
India's solar transition extends beyond large-scale power plants. Through dedicated schemes for households and farmers, solar is improving energy access, reducing electricity costs, and creating new livelihood opportunities.
PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana
Launched on 13 February 2024 with an outlay of ₹75,021 crore, PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana brings rooftop solar benefits directly to households nationwide. It is the world's largest domestic rooftop solar programme. Eligible households receive subsidies for rooftop solar installations, while collateral-free loans facilitate adoption. The scheme is implemented through a dedicated national portal, enabling seamless registration, installation, and subsidy disbursement.
Key Achievements
About
65 lakh households
were solarised as of November 2026.
₹
28,024 crore
disbursed as Central Financial Assistance till July 2026.
Over
21 lakh households
received zero electricity bills as of November 2026.
The scheme enables households to generate their own electricity. It reduces electricity bills and promotes rooftop solar adoption. PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana has also received international support, with the World Bank approving financing to help scale up residential rooftop solar adoption in India.
From High Electricity Bills to Solar Savings
On learning about the PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana, Sudhanshu Dubey, a resident of Jawar Colony in Gwalior, opted for rooftop solar.
The installation and subsidy process were completed smoothly, and the subsidy amount was credited directly to his bank account. For more than a year now, the benefits have been visible every month. Earlier, his household electricity bill often exceeded ₹10,000; today, it is almost negligible. The rooftop solar system continues to generate power reliably, helping the family meet its electricity needs while reducing monthly expenses.
For Sudhanshu, the scheme has turned sunlight into savings. His experience reflects how PM Surya Ghar is enabling households across the country to adopt clean energy and gain greater control over their electricity costs.
Pradhan Mantri-Kisan Urja Suraksha Evam Utthaan Mahabhiyan (PM-KUSUM)
Launched in 2019, the PM-KUSUM seeks to expand the use of solar energy in agriculture. The scheme supports the installation of decentralised solar power plants, standalone solar agriculture pumps, and the solarisation of grid-connected agricultural pumps. It aims to provide reliable daytime power for irrigation, reduce dependence on diesel, and enhance income opportunities for farmers.
PM-KUSUM enables farmers to harness solar energy both for irrigation and power generation. Under the scheme, farmers install solar pumps for irrigation and sell surplus electricity to distribution companies, where eligible. The scheme is focused on adding around
34,800 MW
of solar capacity by 2026-27, with Central financial support of
₹34,422 crore
.

Nearly
11.91 lakh off-grid solar pumps
installed for agricultural use.
More than
17.18 lakh agricultural pumps
are covered through feeder-level solarisation.
Around
2,426 MW
of decentralised solar power capacity commissioned on farmers’ land.
Over
21.77 lakh farmers
benefited across the country, as of 31 December 2025.
Both schemes have emerged as an important pillar of India's distributed solar energy landscape.
In FY 2025–26, distributed solar solutions contributed
16.3 GW
, or
36%
, of the
44.61 GW
of solar capacity added during the year. Of this,
7.6 GW
came from PM-KUSUM and
8.7 GW
from rooftop solar.
India's Growing Leadership in Global Solar Cooperation
India's leadership in solar energy extends beyond its borders. The country is strengthening international cooperation, technology exchange, and capacity building.
International Solar Alliance (ISA):
Co-founded by India and France at COP21 in Paris in 2015, the ISA has emerged as a key platform for global solar cooperation. The Alliance brings together countries including the Maldives, Greece, Germany, Italy, Bhutan, Luxembourg, and Argentina to accelerate solar deployment, share knowledge and technology. The ISA has evolved into an important platform for cooperation among member countries.
One Sun One World One Grid (OSOWOG):
Proposed by India in 2018, OSOWOG is a vision for an interconnected global renewable energy network. To advance this vision, India and the United Kingdom launched the
Green Grids Initiative–One Sun One World One Grid (GGI–OSOWOG) at COP26 in 2021.
The initiative is supported by Australia, France, the United States, and the International Solar Alliance. It promotes cross-border RE trade through interconnected electricity grids, strengthening energy security and accelerating the clean energy transition.
Through the ISA and other partnerships, India has strengthened renewable energy cooperation across the Global South. During its G20 Presidency, India also helped build consensus on tripling global renewable energy capacity by 2030.
The Road Ahead
India's achievements in the solar market reflect sustained policy support, expanding manufacturing, strengthened infrastructure, and growing public participation. As India progresses towards its Panchamrit commitments and net-zero target by 2070, solar power will remain a key pillar. It will continue to drive the clean energy transition.
